There is no difference, the names are interchangeable
body.explanation: The lecture compares them directly: a chalazion is a blocked meibomian gland within the lid, while a stye is a blocked oil gland on the edge of the eyelid.

title: Which cranial nerves carry parasympathetic fibres?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cranial nerves carry parasympathetic fibres?
body.explanation: Remember 3, 7, 9, 10. In the orbit it is CN III that carries the parasympathetic supply, through the ciliary ganglion.

title: What divides the cochlear canal into scala vestibuli and scala tympani?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What divides the cochlear canal into scala vestibuli and scala tympani?
body.explanation: A spiral ridge of bone, the spiral lamina, projects from the modiolus like the thread of a screw and partly divides the canal into scala vestibuli above and scala tympani below.
option_notes: The modiolus is the core.
The helicotrema is where they join.
The bony spiral lamina (with the basilar membrane) divides the canal.
The stria vascularis makes endolymph.

title: What forms the posterior wall of the oropharynx?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the posterior wall of the oropharynx?
body.explanation: In the oropharynx the posterior wall is the superior pharyngeal constrictor; in the laryngopharynx it is the middle and inferior constrictors.

title: Which extraocular muscle arises from the anterior part of the floor of the orbit?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which extraocular muscle arises from the anterior part of the floor of the orbit?
body.explanation: The inferior oblique arises from the anterior part of the floor of the orbit (the maxilla), posterior and temporo-inferior quadrant, and inserts into the sclera deep to the lateral rectus muscle.

title: What is white matter mainly made of?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is white matter mainly made of?
body.explanation: White matter is myelinated axons; grey matter is cell bodies, dendrites and synapses.
option_notes: Myelin gives the white colour.
Cell bodies form grey matter.
These are grey matter.
They line the ventricles.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the internal carotid. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: What is the extent of the cervical enlargement?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the extent of the cervical enlargement?
body.explanation: The cervical enlargement (C4 to T1) supplies the upper limbs; the lumbar enlargement (L1 to S3) the lower limbs.
option_notes: Thoracic.
Lumbosacral enlargement.
C4 to T1, for the brachial plexus.
Too high.

title: How is hydrocephalus commonly treated by diverting CSF away from the brain?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How is hydrocephalus commonly treated by diverting CSF away from the brain?
options: Removing the choroid plexus in every patient
body.explanation: A shunt diverts excess CSF away from the brain, for example to the peritoneal cavity.
option_notes: A VP shunt drains CSF to the peritoneum.
Not a routine treatment.
Not a long-term treatment.
Antibiotics treat infection, not hydrocephalus itself.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Facial nerve (VII): the nerve running through the temporal bone in its own canal, close to the middle ear.
option_notes: Cochlea is the snail-shaped hearing organ of the inner ear.
Vestibule and semicircular canals is the balance part of the bony labyrinth: the central vestibule and the three looped canals.
Incus is the middle ossicle, between malleus and stapes.
The nerve running through the temporal bone in its own canal, close to the middle ear.

title: Which muscle does the trochlear nerve supply?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscle does the trochlear nerve supply?
body.explanation: CN III supplies the superior, inferior and medial recti, the inferior oblique and levator palpebrae superioris; CN IV the superior oblique; CN VI the lateral rectus.

title: Which duct opens on the papilla beside the frenulum of the tongue?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which duct opens on the papilla beside the frenulum of the tongue?
options: The parotid duct of the cheek
body.explanation: On each side of the frenulum, a small papilla has the opening of the duct of the submandibular gland. A rounded ridge extending backward and laterally from the papilla is produced by the sublingual gland.

title: Which artery arises from the front of the external carotid just below the greater cornu of the hyoid and supplies the thyroid gland?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which artery arises from the front of the external carotid just below the greater cornu of the hyoid and supplies the thyroid gland?
body.explanation: The superior thyroid artery arises from the front of the external carotid below the tip of the greater cornu of the hyoid, and divides into infrahyoid, superior laryngeal, cricothyroid and glandular branches.

title: Which arteries supply the external ear?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which arteries supply the external ear?
options: Branches of the internal carotid artery
body.explanation: The external ear is supplied by the superficial temporal and posterior auricular arteries, both branches of the external carotid.
option_notes: Superficial temporal and posterior auricular arteries supply it.
These supply the face and tongue.
Not the main supply.
The external ear is supplied by external carotid branches.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
options: Triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus
body.explanation: Temporal pole: the front tip of the temporal lobe.
option_notes: Paracentral lobule is the medial continuation of the precentral and postcentral gyri (leg area).
Triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus is the middle, triangle-shaped part of the inferior frontal gyrus, part of Broca's area.
The front tip of the temporal lobe.
Lingual gyrus is the medial occipital gyrus below the calcarine sulcus.

title: Which cells produce the mucin layer of the tear film?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cells produce the mucin layer of the tear film?
options: Sebaceous glands of Zeis, at the lashes
body.explanation: The mucin layer is produced by the goblet cells of the conjunctiva. It attaches the tear film to the eye and spreads the water evenly.

title: Which muscle is supplied by the abducens nerve (CN VI)?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscle is supplied by the abducens nerve (CN VI)?
body.explanation: LR6 SO4: lateral rectus is supplied by CN VI, superior oblique by CN IV, and every other extraocular muscle (including levator palpebrae superioris) by CN III.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the nasal bones. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: What lies in the posterior part of the submandibular triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What lies in the posterior part of the submandibular triangle?
options: The submental artery below the gland
body.explanation: In the posterior part lies the external carotid artery, ascending deep into the substance of the parotid gland. Beneath the gland, on the surface of mylohyoid, are the submental artery and the mylohyoid nerve and vessels (anterior part).
option_notes: Submental artery lies in the anterior part, beneath the gland on mylohyoid.
Mylohyoid nerve and vessels lie in the anterior part, on mylohyoid.
The accessory nerve crosses the posterior (occipital) triangle, not the submandibular triangle.
Correct: the external carotid artery ascends into the parotid gland in the posterior part.

title: Which muscles are supplied by the oculomotor nerve (CN III)? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscles are supplied by the oculomotor nerve (CN III)? (choose all)
body.explanation: LR6 SO4: lateral rectus is CN VI and superior oblique is CN IV. Everything else, including the inferior oblique and levator palpebrae superioris, is CN III.

title: What features mark a spinal cord compression syndrome?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What features mark a spinal cord compression syndrome?
body.explanation: Compression is a neurosurgical emergency with a localized lesion syndrome, a sublesional syndrome and a spinal syndrome.
option_notes: Signs at the lesion level.
Signs below the lesion.
Not a feature.
Not a feature.

title: Which canal does the aqueous enter after crossing the trabecular meshwork?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which canal does the aqueous enter after crossing the trabecular meshwork?
body.explanation: Aqueous traverses the trabecular meshwork, crosses the inner wall of Schlemm's canal, then passes into collector channels, aqueous veins and episcleral veins.

title: The abducens nucleus contains motor neurons and which other cell type?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The abducens nucleus contains motor neurons and which other cell type?
options: Sensory relay neurons from the retina
Pretectal neurons for the light reflex
body.explanation: The abducens nucleus contains motor neurons controlling the lateral rectus on the same side, and interneurons that cross the midline to the contralateral oculomotor nucleus, which controls the medial rectus of the opposite eye.

title: How many bones make up the human skull, counting the mandible?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How many bones make up the human skull, counting the mandible?
body.explanation: 22 bones: 8 cranial (neurocranium) and 14 facial (viscerocranium, which includes the mandible).

title: Which intrinsic muscle is unpaired?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which intrinsic muscle is unpaired?
body.explanation: All the intrinsic muscles of the larynx are paired except the transverse arytenoid (interarytenoid), which is unpaired.
option_notes: Paired.
The transverse arytenoid crosses the midline and is single.
Paired.
Paired.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Caudate nucleus: the C-shaped nucleus curving along the lateral ventricle.
option_notes: The C-shaped nucleus curving along the lateral ventricle.
Amygdala is the almond-shaped nucleus in front of the hippocampus, at the tip of the temporal horn: emotion.
Putamen is the outer part of the lentiform nucleus.
Globus pallidus is the inner part of the lentiform nucleus, medial to the putamen.

title: According to the lecture, how much of the posterior segment does the vitreous body fill?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: According to the lecture, how much of the posterior segment does the vitreous body fill?
body.explanation: The lecture describes the vitreous body as a jelly-like substance filling up 80 percent of the posterior segment (vitreous chamber). It transmits light and holds the retina and lens in place.
option_notes: Correct: the figure given on the lecture slide.
Wrong: far too small for the vitreous body.
Wrong: not the lecture's figure.
Wrong per the lecture, which gives 80 percent.

title: An expanding pituitary tumour compressing the optic chiasma causes which defect?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: An expanding pituitary tumour compressing the optic chiasma causes which defect?
body.explanation: The pituitary sits beneath the chiasm, so it compresses the crossing nasal fibres, which carry the temporal halves of both visual fields.

title: What is papilloedema?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is papilloedema?
body.explanation: Papilloedema is optic disc swelling secondary to raised intracranial pressure, because the subarachnoid space continues along the optic nerve sheath.

title: What does the aqueduct of the cochlea connect?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the aqueduct of the cochlea connect?
body.explanation: The aqueduct of the cochlea is a narrow canal through which the perilymph of the cochlea communicates with the cerebrospinal fluid.
option_notes: Not this connection.
This is the Eustachian tube.
It links perilymph to the subarachnoid CSF.
The utriculo-saccular duct does this.

title: The lateral pterygoid inserts mainly on which part of the mandible?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The lateral pterygoid inserts mainly on which part of the mandible?
body.explanation: Its two heads insert on the pterygoid fovea of the neck of the condylar process, and on the capsule and articular disc of the temporomandibular joint. It protrudes the mandible.

title: Which drainage route accounts for most aqueous outflow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which drainage route accounts for most aqueous outflow?
options: The uveoscleral route, through the muscle
body.explanation: The trabecular meshwork route accounts for 50 to 75 percent of aqueous drainage. It is pressure sensitive: outflow increases with greater intraocular pressure.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the sphenoid sinus. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Where does the vestibulocochlear nerve divide?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the vestibulocochlear nerve divide?
options: At the cochlear apex, in the canal
body.explanation: CN VIII divides in the internal auditory canal into an anterior branch, the cochlear nerve, and a posterior branch, the vestibular nerve.
option_notes: It splits into cochlear and vestibular parts in the internal auditory canal.
It does not enter the middle ear.
Not at the brainstem.
Not at the apex.

title: The paper-thin lamina papyracea is part of which bone?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The paper-thin lamina papyracea is part of which bone?
body.explanation: Lamina papyracea is the orbital plate of the ethmoid. It forms the largest part of the medial wall and separates the orbit from the ethmoid sinus.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
options: Posterior lobe of the cerebellar hemisphere
body.explanation: Posterior lobe of the cerebellar hemisphere: the large part of the cerebellar hemisphere behind the primary fissure.
option_notes: Flocculus is the small lobule beside the middle cerebellar peduncle, part of the flocculonodular lobe.
Vermis is the midline part of the cerebellum joining the two hemispheres.
Superior cerebellar peduncle is the bundle joining the cerebellum to the midbrain; the main cerebellar output.
The large part of the cerebellar hemisphere behind the primary fissure.

title: What are the tarsal plates made of?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What are the tarsal plates made of?
options: Hyaline cartilage, as in a joint
body.explanation: The superior and inferior tarsi are plates of dense connective tissue that give the eyelid its shape and rigidity, and they contain the tarsal (meibomian) glands.

title: How many walls of the tympanic cavity are bony?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How many walls of the tympanic cavity are bony?
body.explanation: It is a six-sided box: five bony walls, and the sixth, lateral wall membranous, formed by the tympanic membrane.
option_notes: One more.
Five walls are bone; the lateral wall is mostly membrane.
The lateral wall is mostly membrane.
More than three are bony.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Midbrain: the top part of the brainstem, between diencephalon and pons.
option_notes: Superior colliculus is the upper pair of bumps on the back of the midbrain: visual reflexes.
Medulla oblongata is the lowest part of the brainstem, continuous with the spinal cord.
Cerebral peduncle (crus cerebri) is the thick pillar on the front of the midbrain carrying descending fibres.
The top part of the brainstem, between diencephalon and pons.

title: What is the rima glottidis?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the rima glottidis?
options: The space above the vestibular folds
The gap between the arytenoid cartilages
The opening of the laryngeal ventricle
body.explanation: The glottis is delimited by the two vocal cords and is triangular in shape. It is narrower than the vestibular cleft, and a narrow zone in children, where obstructive oedema causes respiratory distress very rapidly.
option_notes: That is the vestibule.
Only part of it.
The gap between the vocal cords.
Not this.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the nasopharynx. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Where do the constrictor muscles insert posteriorly?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where do the constrictor muscles insert posteriorly?
body.explanation: All three constrictors insert into the median fibrous raphe in the midline behind. The superior constrictor also reaches the pharyngeal tubercle on the base of the skull.

title: Name the four refractive media of the eye in order.
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Name the four refractive media of the eye in order.
options: Cornea, lens, aqueous humour, vitreous humour
Cornea, aqueous humour, lens, vitreous humour
body.explanation: The refractive media are the cornea, the aqueous humour, the lens and the vitreous humour.

title: Which structure secretes the aqueous humour?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure secretes the aqueous humour?
body.explanation: The ciliary processes of the ciliary body secrete aqueous humour into the posterior chamber. It is formed by diffusion, ultrafiltration and active secretion.

title: What does the cerebrum consist of?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the cerebrum consist of?
options: The pons and the medulla only
body.explanation: The cerebrum is made of the two cerebral hemispheres (telencephalon) and the diencephalon, which encloses the third ventricle.
option_notes: The cerebrum is the two hemispheres plus the diencephalon.
These lie below and behind it.
The cord is outside the cerebrum.
These are brainstem parts.

title: Which is the smallest part of the brainstem?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which is the smallest part of the brainstem?
body.explanation: The midbrain measures around 2 cm and passes through the tentorial opening. The pons is the largest part.
option_notes: The midbrain is the shortest part.
Larger.
Larger.
Only part of the midbrain.

title: Which structure is the peak of the fourth ventricle, under a cerebellar nucleus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is the peak of the fourth ventricle, under a cerebellar nucleus?
body.explanation: The peak of the fourth ventricle inside the cerebellum is the fastigium, under the fastigial nucleus.
option_notes: The fastigium is the roof's peak.
The obex is the lowest tip.
The rhomboid fossa is the floor.
That is on the midbrain.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the midbrain. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: This is at the arrow: the top of the brainstem, below the diencephalon.
Not at the arrow; this is the oval swelling on the side of the upper medulla.
Not at the arrow; this is the ridge on the front of the medulla carrying corticospinal fibres.
Not at the arrow; this is the two thick pillars on the front of the midbrain.

title: From what do the nasal cavities develop?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: From what do the nasal cavities develop?
body.explanation: The nose and nasal cavities are formed by five facial prominences derived from the first branchial arch, appearing at the end of the fifth week. The nasal cavities derive from the nasal placodes, which invaginate to form the primitive nasal cavity, the primitive olfactory gutter.

title: What joins the two thalami?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What joins the two thalami?
body.explanation: Each thalamus connects to the other via the interthalamic adhesion.
option_notes: Joins the hemispheres.
Joins the temporal lobes.
The interthalamic adhesion crosses the third ventricle.
A projection pathway.

title: Which nuclei make up the dorsal striatum?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nuclei make up the dorsal striatum?
body.explanation: The dorsal striatum is the caudate and putamen; the ventral striatum is the nucleus accumbens and olfactory tubercle.
option_notes: Caudate plus putamen.
These form the lentiform nucleus.
These form the ventral striatum.
These are other basal ganglia.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the retina (both eyes). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: The oral cavity extends from the lips to which structure?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The oral cavity extends from the lips to which structure?
body.explanation: The oral cavity extends from the lips to the oropharyngeal isthmus, the junction of mouth and pharynx. It is subdivided into the vestibule and the oral cavity proper.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the mammillary body. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the narrow midline cavity between the two thalami.
This is at the arrow: the round swelling behind the infundibulum.
Not at the arrow; this is the gland hanging from the infundibulum in the sella.
Not at the arrow; this is the region below the thalamus forming the floor of the third ventricle.

title: How many processes does each maxilla have?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How many processes does each maxilla have?
body.explanation: Each maxilla has a body and four processes: frontal, zygomatic, alveolar and palatine.

title: What is a role of the pontine flexure?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is a role of the pontine flexure?
options: It thins the roof of the fourth ventricle
body.explanation: The pontine flexure thins the roof of the fourth ventricle, makes space for the cerebellum and separates metencephalon from myelencephalon.
option_notes: It thins the fourth ventricle roof.
Closure happens earlier.
They come from the telencephalon.
Not this flexure's role.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the anterior two thirds (oral part). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: The superior orbital fissure lies between which structures?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The superior orbital fissure lies between which structures?
options: Lesser and greater wings of the sphenoid
Greater wing of the sphenoid and maxilla
body.explanation: The superior orbital fissure is the gap between the lesser and greater wings of the sphenoid. The inferior orbital fissure lies between the greater wing of the sphenoid and the maxilla.

title: What does the basal turn of the cochlea form in the middle ear?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the basal turn of the cochlea form in the middle ear?
body.explanation: The cochlear canal spirals around the modiolus, and its basal turn bulges into the tympanic cavity as the promontory.
option_notes: The basal turn bulges as the promontory.
The oval window holds the stapes.
The tegmen is the roof.
The aditus leads to the mastoid.

title: Which three forgotten triangles lie within the submandibular triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which three forgotten triangles lie within the submandibular triangle?
body.explanation: Beclard's, Lesser's and Pirogoff's triangles, also known as the forgotten or smaller triangles of the neck, are housed within the submandibular triangle.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Trachea: the tube of C-shaped cartilage rings below the cricoid.
option_notes: Thyroid cartilage is the large shield-shaped cartilage with the laryngeal prominence.
Cricoid cartilage is the only complete cartilage ring, below the thyroid cartilage.
The tube of C-shaped cartilage rings below the cricoid.
Hyoid bone is the U-shaped bone above the larynx.

title: Which triangle of the neck is unpaired?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which triangle of the neck is unpaired?
body.explanation: The anterior triangle is subdivided into three paired triangles (carotid, submandibular and muscular) and one unpaired triangle, the submental, which lies below the chin between the anterior bellies of digastric of both sides.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the condylar process (head and neck). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which vital functions depend on the brainstem?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which vital functions depend on the brainstem?
body.explanation: The brainstem is responsible for breathing, consciousness, blood pressure, heart rate and sleep.
option_notes: Respiratory centres are in the brainstem.
The reticular formation keeps us conscious.
Cardiovascular centres are in the brainstem.
Reading and writing are cortical functions.

title: The main arterial supply of the lacrimal gland comes from which artery?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The main arterial supply of the lacrimal gland comes from which artery?
options: The lacrimal artery, from the ophthalmic artery
The facial artery, a branch of the external carotid
The infraorbital artery, from the maxillary
body.explanation: The lacrimal artery is derived from the ophthalmic artery, a branch of the internal carotid. Venous drainage is via the superior ophthalmic vein into the cavernous sinus.

title: Who was Pirogoff's triangle named after?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Who was Pirogoff's triangle named after?
options: A French surgeon of the same period
body.explanation: It is named after the Russian surgeon and scientist Nikolai I Pirogoff, who lived from 1810 to 1881 and gave the first description of this area of the neck.

title: How many walls does each nasal cavity have?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How many walls does each nasal cavity have?
body.explanation: Each nasal cavity is shaped like a long sagittal corridor with four walls (roof, floor, medial and lateral) and two apertures, anterior and posterior.

title: The tongue is divided into how many parts, and what are they?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The tongue is divided into how many parts, and what are they?
body.explanation: The tongue is a mass of striated muscles covered with mucous membrane, divided into right and left halves by a median septum. Three parts: oral (anterior two thirds), pharyngeal (posterior third) and root. Two surfaces: dorsal and ventral.

title: What are the two stated functions of the tear film?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What are the two stated functions of the tear film?
options: Focusing light and adjusting the size of the pupil
Draining aqueous humour and lowering eye pressure
Anchoring the eyeball and moving it
Lubricating the eye and protecting it
body.explanation: The tear film is made of water and contains electrolytes and proteins. Its functions are to lubricate the eye and to protect it from infections.

title: Which triangles subdivide the anterior triangle? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which triangles subdivide the anterior triangle? (choose all)
body.explanation: The anterior triangle is subdivided into the carotid, submandibular and muscular triangles, all paired, plus the unpaired submental triangle. The occipital and subclavian triangles subdivide the posterior triangle.

title: What does the ciliary ganglion relay, and through which branches?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the ciliary ganglion relay, and through which branches?
options: Parasympathetic impulses from the oculomotor nerve
Sympathetic impulses only, through the long ciliary nerves
Motor impulses to the extraocular muscles
Taste fibres from the anterior tongue
body.explanation: The ciliary ganglion is a peripheral parasympathetic ganglion relaying parasympathetic impulses from the oculomotor nerve to target structures. It also transports sympathetic impulses from the internal carotid plexus and sensory impulses from the nasociliary nerve. Its branches are the short ciliary nerves.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the trapezius. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which movement at the temporomandibular joint is mostly caused by gravity?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which movement at the temporomandibular joint is mostly caused by gravity?
body.explanation: Elevation and depression happen in the lower part of the joint. Depression is mainly due to gravity, with the digastric, geniohyoid and mylohyoid helping if there is resistance.

title: Which glands lie in the subcutaneous tissue of the eyelid margin? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which glands lie in the subcutaneous tissue of the eyelid margin? (choose all)
body.explanation: The sebaceous glands of Zeis and the ciliary glands of Moll (modified apocrine sweat glands) sit at the lid margin and contribute sebum to the lipid film across the anterior chamber of the eye.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the left lobe (lateral lobe). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: This is at the arrow: the lateral lobe on the patient's left (viewer's right).
Not at the arrow; this is the external carotid branch reaching the upper pole.
Not at the arrow; this is the lateral lobe on the patient's right (viewer's left).
Not at the arrow; this is the large shield-shaped cartilage of the larynx (Adam's apple).

title: Which muscles are extrinsic muscles of the tongue? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscles are extrinsic muscles of the tongue? (choose all)
body.explanation: The four extrinsic muscles are palatoglossus, genioglossus, hyoglossus and styloglossus. The mylohyoid forms the floor of the mouth and the buccinator the cheek.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the common carotid. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which of these is NOT one of the four main branches of the lingual artery?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the four main branches of the lingual artery?
body.explanation: The four main branches of the lingual artery are the suprahyoid, dorsal lingual, sublingual and deep lingual. The ascending palatine is a branch of the facial artery.

title: Where does lymph from the head and neck finally return to the bloodstream?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does lymph from the head and neck finally return to the bloodstream?
options: The great veins at the root of the neck
The cisterna chyli in the upper abdomen
The spleen and the red pulp
body.explanation: From the deep and superficial cervical nodes, lymph travels to the supraclavicular nodes and then enters the large veins at the root of the neck through the jugular trunks, emptying into the thoracic duct on the left or the right lymphatic duct.

title: Roughly how thick is the eyelid?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Roughly how thick is the eyelid?
body.explanation: The lecture gives the thickness of the eyelid as 2 to 3 mm.

title: What may be found within Pirogoff's triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What may be found within Pirogoff's triangle?
body.explanation: The lingual artery can sometimes be found in Pirogoff's triangle, underneath the fibres of the hyoglossus muscle. The triangle is also considered the posterior continuation of Lesser's triangle.

title: Which artery supplies the supraglottic larynx?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which artery supplies the supraglottic larynx?
options: The posteroinferior laryngeal artery, from the inferior thyroid
The superior laryngeal artery, from the superior thyroid artery
The lingual artery, from the external carotid
body.explanation: Superior laryngeal artery, a branch of the superior thyroid artery, supplies the supraglottic part. The anteroinferior laryngeal artery supplies the anterior infraglottic stage. The posteroinferior laryngeal artery, from the inferior thyroid artery, supplies the posterior laryngeal mucosa.
option_notes: That supplies below the cords.
The superior laryngeal artery (from the superior thyroid).
Supplies the tongue.
Not the main supply.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the external carotid. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
options: Primary motor cortex (precentral gyrus, Betz cells)
body.explanation: The arrow points to the pyramidal decussation (about 90% cross). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the tympanic cavity (middle ear). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the opening closed by the stapes footplate.
Not at the arrow; this is the thin membrane closing the inner end of the canal.
Not at the arrow; this is the cartilage flap outside the head that collects sound.
This is at the arrow: the air space behind the eardrum holding the ossicles.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Superior temporal gyrus: the top gyrus of the temporal lobe, under the lateral sulcus; its back part holds Wernicke's area.
option_notes: Insula is the cortex hidden deep in the lateral sulcus, covered by the opercula.
Supramarginal gyrus is the parietal gyrus arching around the end of the lateral sulcus.
Temporal pole is the front tip of the temporal lobe.
The top gyrus of the temporal lobe, under the lateral sulcus; its back part holds Wernicke's area.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
options: Triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus
body.explanation: Superior parietal lobule: the parietal area above the intraparietal sulcus.
option_notes: Cuneus is the wedge of medial occipital cortex between the calcarine and parieto-occipital sulci.
Precuneus is the medial parietal area in front of the parieto-occipital sulcus.
The parietal area above the intraparietal sulcus.
Triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus is the middle, triangle-shaped part of the inferior frontal gyrus, part of Broca's area.

title: Which three types of fibre pass through the ciliary ganglion?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which three types of fibre pass through the ciliary ganglion?
options: Parasympathetic and motor fibres only, no others
body.explanation: In the lecture's colour diagram: green for parasympathetic, red for sympathetic and blue for sensory. The parasympathetic fibres synapse there; the sympathetic and sensory fibres pass straight through.

title: Which cranial nerve is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cranial nerve is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Facial nerve (VII): leaves at the cerebellopontine angle, with VIII.
option_notes: Leaves at the cerebellopontine angle, with VIII.
Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) is leaves the medulla behind the olive, above the vagus.
Oculomotor nerve (III) is leaves the midbrain between the cerebral peduncles.
Optic nerve (II) is runs from the eye to the optic chiasm.

title: What is the primary action of the superior oblique?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the primary action of the superior oblique?
body.explanation: SO: intorsion, depression, abduction. IO: extorsion, elevation, abduction. That pair is the mirror image of each other.

title: Which cranial nerve is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cranial nerve is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Trigeminal nerve (V): the large nerve leaving the side of the pons.
option_notes: Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) is leaves the medulla behind the olive, above the vagus.
Vagus nerve (X) is leaves the medulla behind the olive, below IX.
Hypoglossal nerve (XII) is leaves the medulla between the pyramid and the olive.
The large nerve leaving the side of the pons.

title: Which is described as the only true pedicle of each lobe?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which is described as the only true pedicle of each lobe?
body.explanation: The superior thyroid pedicle is the only true pedicle of each lobe, approaching the superior pole of the lateral lobe. It is made of the superior thyroid artery and veins.
option_notes: The superior pedicle is the only true pedicle.
Not described as the true pedicle.
A vein, not the pedicle.
Inconstant.

title: Which two cranial nerves supply the nasal cavity?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which two cranial nerves supply the nasal cavity?
body.explanation: Innervation is provided by branches of V and I: sensory nerves from V (the spheno-palatine nerve from V2 and the internal nasal nerve) and the olfactory nerves (CN I).

title: Which are signs locating a cerebral lesion?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are signs locating a cerebral lesion?
body.explanation: Aphasia, blindness, hemiplegia, behavioural disorders and epilepsy are localising signs of a cerebral lesion.
option_notes: Aphasia points to the dominant hemisphere.
Hemiplegia can come from a cerebral lesion.
Usually ear or nerve VIII, not the cerebrum.
Brainstem (IX, X).

title: Which receptor do somatic motor neurons act on?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which receptor do somatic motor neurons act on?
body.explanation: A single somatic motor neuron runs from the ventral horn to skeletal muscle, releasing acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors, with no ganglion in between.

title: What forms the superior border of Lesser's triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the superior border of Lesser's triangle?
options: The greater cornu of the hyoid
body.explanation: Lesser's triangle is bounded by the hypoglossal nerve superiorly, the anterior belly and intermediate tendon of digastric inferiorly, and the posterior margin of mylohyoid posteriorly. Its floor is formed by hyoglossus and mylohyoid.

title: Which are the three primary brain vesicles?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are the three primary brain vesicles?
body.explanation: The three primary vesicles (week 4) are the forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain.
option_notes: Forebrain, midbrain, hindbrain.
These are secondary vesicles.
These are secondary vesicles.
These are adult parts.

title: Which nuclei form the interposed nuclei?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nuclei form the interposed nuclei?
body.explanation: The interposed nuclei consist of the globose and emboliform nuclei.
option_notes: Globose + emboliform.
These are the lateral and medial nuclei.
The fastigial is separate.
The dentate is separate.

title: What is spinal cord compression considered?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is spinal cord compression considered?
body.explanation: Spinal cord compression is a neurosurgical emergency, recognised by lesion, sublesional and spinal syndromes.
option_notes: It needs urgent neurosurgical care.
Delay risks permanent paralysis.
It is a neurological problem.
It is a spinal, not cerebellar, syndrome.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the coronoid process: temporalis insertion. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which are actions of the buccinator? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are actions of the buccinator? (choose all)
options: Keeping food between the teeth while chewing
Helping to blow air out of the mouth
body.explanation: The buccinator compresses the cheek, keeping food under the teeth, and expels air from the distended cheeks, as in blowing a trumpet. Neonates use it to suckle.

title: Sensory innervation of the lacrimal gland is carried by which nerve?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Sensory innervation of the lacrimal gland is carried by which nerve?
options: The zygomatic nerve, a branch of V2
The greater petrosal nerve, from CN VII
body.explanation: The sensory fibres travel in the lacrimal nerve, a branch of the ophthalmic nerve, which is itself derived from the trigeminal nerve.

title: What separates the tympanic cavity from the middle cranial fossa?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What separates the tympanic cavity from the middle cranial fossa?
body.explanation: The roof, the tegmen tympani, is a thin plate of bone separating the tympanic cavity from the middle cranial fossa.
option_notes: The jugular bulb lies below the floor.
The tegmen tympani is the thin bony roof.
The promontory is on the medial wall.
The aditus opens backwards.

title: Which cavity does the diencephalon surround?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cavity does the diencephalon surround?
body.explanation: The diencephalon lies around the third ventricle; the thalami form its lateral walls and the hypothalamus its floor.
option_notes: The third ventricle lies in the middle of the diencephalon.
The fourth ventricle lies behind the pons and medulla.
The lateral ventricles are in the hemispheres.
The central canal is in the spinal cord.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the submandibular triangle. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: What does the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve supply?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve supply?
options: Motor supply to all intrinsic muscles
body.explanation: The internal branch pierces the thyrohyoid membrane and gives sensory innervation to the supraglottic mucosa, plus autonomic fibres. The recurrent laryngeal nerve gives sensation below the vocal folds.
option_notes: It is sensory above the vocal folds.
That is the recurrent nerve.
That is the recurrent nerve.
That is the external branch.

title: Which cranial nerves do NOT arise from the brainstem?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cranial nerves do NOT arise from the brainstem?
body.explanation: All cranial nerves arise from the brainstem except CN I and CN II.
option_notes: Medulla.
I and II are not brainstem nerves.
Midbrain.
Pontine region.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the thyrohyoid membrane. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the complete ring below the thyroid cartilage.
This is at the arrow: the sheet joining the hyoid to the thyroid cartilage.
Not at the arrow; this is the large shield-shaped cartilage of the larynx (Adam's apple).
Not at the arrow; this is the tube of C-shaped rings below the cricoid.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Middle frontal gyrus: the middle horizontal gyrus of the lateral frontal lobe.
option_notes: Paracentral lobule is the medial continuation of the precentral and postcentral gyri (leg area).
Insula is the cortex hidden deep in the lateral sulcus, covered by the opercula.
Superior temporal gyrus is the top gyrus of the temporal lobe, under the lateral sulcus; its back part holds Wernicke's area.
The middle horizontal gyrus of the lateral frontal lobe.

title: Which functional area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which functional area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: The opercular and triangular parts of the inferior frontal gyrus form Broca's area on the dominant side.
option_notes: Broca's area (speech production) lies in the opercular and triangular parts of the inferior frontal gyrus.
Primary motor cortex lies in the precentral gyrus.
Primary somatosensory cortex lies in the postcentral gyrus.
Primary visual cortex lies in the banks of the calcarine sulcus.

title: Which branches arise from the superior vestibular nerve?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which branches arise from the superior vestibular nerve?
body.explanation: Superior vestibular nerve: utricular, superior ampullary and lateral ampullary nerves. The saccular nerve comes from the inferior vestibular nerve.
option_notes: The utricular nerve is superior.
The lateral ampullary nerve is superior.
The saccular nerve is inferior.
The cochlear nerve is separate.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the laryngeal prominence (adam’s apple). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: This is at the arrow: the forward bulge where the two thyroid laminae meet.
Not at the arrow; this is the tube of C-shaped rings below the cricoid.
Not at the arrow; this is the sheet joining the hyoid to the thyroid cartilage.
Not at the arrow; this is the V-shaped notch at the top of the thyroid cartilage.

title: What opens into the inferior meatus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What opens into the inferior meatus?
body.explanation: The inferior meatus lies close to the floor of the nasal cavity and receives the opening of the nasolacrimal duct.

title: Where does the sphenoidal sinus open?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the sphenoidal sinus open?
options: Into the middle nasal meatus, in front
body.explanation: The sphenoidal sinus opens at the sphenoidal ostium into the spheno-ethmoidal recess, above the superior concha.

title: Through which opening does the ophthalmic artery enter the orbit?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Through which opening does the ophthalmic artery enter the orbit?
body.explanation: It passes through the optic canal, travels along the medial wall of the orbit and divides into its terminal branches.

title: Where do the longitudinal muscles insert?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where do the longitudinal muscles insert?
body.explanation: Stylopharyngeus, palatopharyngeus and salpingopharyngeus all insert on the posterior border of the thyroid lamina. They elevate the larynx and shorten the pharynx during swallowing.

title: What lies above the roof of the nasal cavity, from front to back?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What lies above the roof of the nasal cavity, from front to back?
options: Orbit, ethmoid cells and maxillary sinus
body.explanation: Relations of the roof, front to back: the frontal sinus, the anterior cerebral fossa and the sphenoidal sinus. The choana relates to the rhinopharynx.

title: Which muscle of mastication inserts on the coronoid process of the mandible?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscle of mastication inserts on the coronoid process of the mandible?
body.explanation: The temporalis arises from the floor of the temporal fossa and the deep temporal fascia and inserts on the coronoid process and anterior border of the ramus. Its posterior fibres retract the mandible.

title: Which dural fold separates the cerebrum from the cerebellum?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which dural fold separates the cerebrum from the cerebellum?
body.explanation: A horizontal extension of the dura, the tentorium, divides the cranial cavity into a supratentorial level (cerebrum) and an infratentorial level (cerebellum and brainstem).
option_notes: The tentorium forms the roof over the cerebellum.
The falx cerebri separates the two hemispheres.
The falx cerebelli separates the cerebellar hemispheres.
The diaphragma sellae covers the pituitary.

title: What does the vermis mainly control?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the vermis mainly control?
body.explanation: The vermis controls axial muscles, posture and gait; the hemispheres coordinate limb movements.
option_notes: The midline controls the trunk and gait.
Fine limb movement depends on the hemispheres.
Vision is the occipital lobe.
Comprehension is Wernicke's area.

title: What bounds the oropharyngeal isthmus above and below?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What bounds the oropharyngeal isthmus above and below?
options: The hard palate above, the floor of the mouth below
The uvula above, the epiglottis below
body.explanation: It is bounded above by the soft palate and the palatoglossal folds, and below by the dorsum of the tongue.

title: At what level does the adult spinal cord end?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: At what level does the adult spinal cord end?
body.explanation: At 6 months of fetal life it reaches S1, at birth L3, and in adults the L1/L2 intervertebral disc.
option_notes: Too low; that is the dural sac.
The adult cord ends at L1/L2.
Too low; the newborn level.
Too high.

title: Where does the pharynx drain its lymph?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the pharynx drain its lymph?
options: The submental nodes of the chin
body.explanation: Lymphatics drain into the jugulodigastric node, also called the tonsillar node.

title: What are the two components of the central nervous system?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What are the two components of the central nervous system?
body.explanation: The CNS consists of two major components: the brain and the spinal cord.
option_notes: The CNS is the brain and spinal cord.
Cranial nerves belong to the PNS.
Spinal nerves belong to the PNS.
Nerves and ganglia are the PNS.

title: What carries sensation from the upper pharynx?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What carries sensation from the upper pharynx?
body.explanation: Sensory innervation: the upper pharynx by the maxillary nerve (V2) and the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX); the lower pharynx by the vagus nerve (CN X).

title: Where does the neural layer of the retina end anteriorly?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the neural layer of the retina end anteriorly?
options: At the optic disc, at the back
body.explanation: The neural layer is light-receptive and ends anteriorly along the ora serrata. The pigmented cell layer is a single layer of cells that absorbs light to reduce scattering within the eye.

title: What connects the tympanic cavity to the mastoid?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What connects the tympanic cavity to the mastoid?
body.explanation: The posterior wall presents the aditus ad antrum, and the vertical part of the facial canal runs in it behind the pyramid down to the stylomastoid foramen.
option_notes: The tube goes to the nasopharynx.
The aditus leads back to the mastoid antrum.
The oval window opens into the inner ear.
Not this connection.

title: What bounds the third ventricle posteriorly, from top to bottom?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What bounds the third ventricle posteriorly, from top to bottom?
options: Habenular commissure, pineal gland, posterior commissure
body.explanation: Posteriorly: habenular commissure, pineal gland and posterior commissure.
option_notes: Posterior wall, top to bottom.
These form the floor.
These are at the front.
These are the diencephalic parts, not a wall.

title: Conjunctivitis affects which layer of the eye?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Conjunctivitis affects which layer of the eye?
body.explanation: Conjunctivitis, also known as pink eye, affects the outer layer, while uveitis affects the middle layer. Uveitis may result from inflammation associated with an autoimmune disorder; conjunctivitis is typically bacterial, viral or fungal.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Middle temporal gyrus: the middle gyrus of the lateral temporal lobe.
option_notes: The middle gyrus of the lateral temporal lobe.
Cuneus is the wedge of medial occipital cortex between the calcarine and parieto-occipital sulci.
Insula is the cortex hidden deep in the lateral sulcus, covered by the opercula.
Gyrus rectus (straight gyrus) is the straight gyrus on the orbital surface, beside the midline.

title: Which layer of the neural tube becomes the grey matter?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which layer of the neural tube becomes the grey matter?
body.explanation: Ventricular zone: innermost, giving neuroblasts and glioblasts. Mantle zone: becomes grey matter. Marginal zone: outermost, becomes white matter.
option_notes: Becomes white matter.
The mantle zone becomes grey matter.
Lines the canal (ependyma).
Gives sensory ganglia.

title: Which plexuses make up the enteric nervous system? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which plexuses make up the enteric nervous system? (choose all)
body.explanation: The myenteric plexus controls motility; the submucosal plexus regulates secretion and blood flow.

title: A patient with a hypothalamic tumour has abnormal body temperature, thirst and appetite. Why?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: A patient with a hypothalamic tumour has abnormal body temperature, thirst and appetite. Why?
options: The hypothalamus controls homeostasis: temperature, hunger and thirst
The pineal gland controls these functions
body.explanation: The hypothalamus maintains a steady internal state: hunger, thirst, body temperature, blood pressure and heart rate.
option_notes: These are hypothalamic homeostatic functions.
The thalamus relays sensation but does not regulate these.
The pineal mainly controls the sleep rhythm.
The cerebellum coordinates movement.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Pineal gland: the small midline gland above the superior colliculi; secretes melatonin.
option_notes: Lateral geniculate body is the thalamic relay for vision.
The small midline gland above the superior colliculi; secretes melatonin.
Thalamus is the large paired grey mass of the diencephalon, the sensory relay.
Optic chiasm is where the optic nerves meet and partly cross, in front of the hypothalamus.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Superior frontal gyrus: the top gyrus of the frontal lobe, running front to back beside the longitudinal fissure.
option_notes: The top gyrus of the frontal lobe, running front to back beside the longitudinal fissure.
Superior temporal gyrus is the top gyrus of the temporal lobe, under the lateral sulcus; its back part holds Wernicke's area.
Paracentral lobule is the medial continuation of the precentral and postcentral gyri (leg area).
Middle temporal gyrus is the middle gyrus of the lateral temporal lobe.

title: Which structures does the ascending pharyngeal artery supply, according to the lecture? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structures does the ascending pharyngeal artery supply, according to the lecture? (choose all)
options: The pharynx and its constrictor muscles
The medial wall of the middle ear
body.explanation: Its three named branches are pharyngeal (pharynx, constrictors, stylopharyngeus, soft palate, tonsils, auditory tube), inferior tympanic (medial wall of the middle ear) and meningeal (dura mater and cranial nerves).

title: Where does the right recurrent laryngeal nerve arise?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the right recurrent laryngeal nerve arise?
options: At the base of the skull
body.explanation: On the right it originates from the vagus at the level of the right subclavian artery, approaches the right oesophageal angle, passes in front of the branches of the inferior thyroid artery, then under the fibres of the inferior constrictor.
option_notes: That is the left nerve.
The right nerve hooks around the right subclavian artery.
Not at the skull base.
Not at the bifurcation.

title: Where does the abducens nerve emerge?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the abducens nerve emerge?
body.explanation: CN V from the lateral mid-pons; CN VI at the pontomedullary junction near the midline; CN VII at the cerebellopontine angle; CN VIII lateral to CN VII.
option_notes: VII and VIII.
That is V.
That is III.
VI emerges at the pontomedullary junction.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
options: Triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus
body.explanation: Lingual gyrus: the medial occipital gyrus below the calcarine sulcus.
option_notes: The medial occipital gyrus below the calcarine sulcus.
Postcentral gyrus is the gyrus just behind the central sulcus: the primary somatosensory cortex.
Precentral gyrus is the gyrus just in front of the central sulcus: the primary motor cortex.
Triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus is the middle, triangle-shaped part of the inferior frontal gyrus, part of Broca's area.

title: Which veins unite to form the angular vein? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which veins unite to form the angular vein? (choose all)
body.explanation: The supratrochlear and supraorbital veins merge at the medial angle of the eye to form the angular vein, which becomes the facial vein.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
options: Triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus
body.explanation: Fusiform (lateral occipitotemporal) gyrus: the gyrus on the inferior surface between the inferior temporal and parahippocampal gyri.
option_notes: The gyrus on the inferior surface between the inferior temporal and parahippocampal gyri.
Paracentral lobule is the medial continuation of the precentral and postcentral gyri (leg area).
Temporal pole is the front tip of the temporal lobe.
Triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus is the middle, triangle-shaped part of the inferior frontal gyrus, part of Broca's area.

title: Where are the respiratory and cardiovascular centres mainly located?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where are the respiratory and cardiovascular centres mainly located?
body.explanation: The respiratory and cardiovascular centres are in the medulla, which is why medullary compression is life-threatening.
option_notes: The medulla holds the vital centres.
The midbrain holds visual and auditory reflex centres.
The thalamus is a sensory relay.
The cerebellum coordinates movement.

title: Which bone contains the sella turcica, the fossa that holds the pituitary gland?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which bone contains the sella turcica, the fossa that holds the pituitary gland?
body.explanation: The sella turcica is a saddle-shaped depression on the upper surface of the body of the sphenoid.

title: What forms the floor of the third ventricle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the floor of the third ventricle?
body.explanation: The hypothalamus lies below the thalamus and makes up the floor of the third ventricle, ending in the infundibulum to the pituitary.
option_notes: The thalamus forms the side walls.
The hypothalamus forms the floor.
The epithalamus is at the back.
Too high.

title: What is the vallecula of the cerebellum?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the vallecula of the cerebellum?
options: A deep median groove on the inferior surface that houses the brainstem
The peak of the fourth ventricle
The space between the two tonsils and the foramen magnum
A fissure on the superior surface
body.explanation: The inferior surface is separated by the vallecula, a deep median groove that houses the brainstem.
option_notes: A median groove holding the brainstem.
That is the fastigium.
Not this.
It is on the inferior surface.

title: What separates the two choanae?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What separates the two choanae?
options: The horizontal plate of the palate
body.explanation: The posterior orifice is the choana: oval with a large vertical axis, limited above by the body of the sphenoid, below by the horizontal plate of the palate, laterally by the pterygoid process, and medially by the vomer, which separates the two choanae.

title: Where does auricularis posterior arise?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does auricularis posterior arise?
body.explanation: The anterior and superior auricular muscles arise from the epicranial aponeurosis; the posterior arises from the mastoid process and inserts into the eminentia conchae.
option_notes: That is the origin of auricularis superior and anterior.
Auricularis posterior arises from the mastoid process.
Not its origin.
The tragus is part of the ear itself.

title: Which flexure is temporary and disappears later in development?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which flexure is temporary and disappears later in development?
body.explanation: The cervical flexure, between hindbrain and spinal cord, is temporary.
option_notes: Temporary.
It persists as the forward bend of the brain.
It shapes the hindbrain.
The cervical flexure disappears.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Arytenoid cartilages: the paired pyramids on the back of the cricoid where the vocal ligaments attach.
option_notes: Epiglottis is the leaf-shaped cartilage behind the tongue base.
The paired pyramids on the back of the cricoid where the vocal ligaments attach.
Hyoid bone is the U-shaped bone above the larynx.
Cricoid cartilage is the only complete cartilage ring, below the thyroid cartilage.

title: Roughly what angle do the lateral walls of the two orbits form with each other?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Roughly what angle do the lateral walls of the two orbits form with each other?
body.explanation: The lateral walls of the two orbits meet at about 90 degrees. The two orbital axes make about 45 degrees with each other, while the medial walls are roughly parallel.

title: Which branch of the posterior auricular artery enters the stylomastoid foramen?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which branch of the posterior auricular artery enters the stylomastoid foramen?
body.explanation: The stylomastoid branch enters the stylomastoid foramen to supply the middle and inner ear and the facial nerve as it exits.

title: Into what do the anterior and posterior spinal veins drain?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Into what do the anterior and posterior spinal veins drain?
options: Radicular veins, then the vertebral venous plexus
Directly into the superior vena cava
body.explanation: Spinal veins drain into radicular veins, then the internal and external vertebral venous plexus.
option_notes: Spinal → radicular → vertebral plexus.
Not directly.
That drains the brain.
That drains the gut.

title: What produces the olive?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What produces the olive?
body.explanation: The pyramid is made by the corticospinal tract; the olive, lateral to it, by the inferior olivary nucleus, important in movement control.
option_notes: Makes the pyramid.
Not this.
The inferior olivary nucleus.
Not here.

title: Which layer of the tear film is produced by the meibomian glands?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which layer of the tear film is produced by the meibomian glands?
body.explanation: Oil layer: meibomian glands, preventing evaporation. Water layer: lacrimal glands, lubricating, allowing blinking, washing away debris and forming a smooth surface. Mucin layer: goblet cells of the conjunctiva, attaching the film to the eye and spreading water evenly.

title: What does the foramen of Pacchioni (tentorial notch) let through?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the foramen of Pacchioni (tentorial notch) let through?
options: The junction between the diencephalon and the midbrain
body.explanation: The small circumference of the tentorium bounds an opening where the diencephalon joins the midbrain.
option_notes: The brainstem passes up through the tentorial notch.
The cord passes through the foramen magnum.
The optic nerves pass through the optic canals.
The vertebral arteries enter through the foramen magnum.

title: Why is the thyroid removed along with its true capsule?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Why is the thyroid removed along with its true capsule?
options: Because the true capsule contains the parathyroid glands
The venous plexus lies deep to it
Because the recurrent nerve runs inside it
Because the false capsule is too thin to hold
body.explanation: The dense venous plexus, unlike that of the prostate gland, lies deep to the true capsule. To avoid haemorrhage during thyroidectomy the gland is removed along with the true capsule.
option_notes: The parathyroids lie outside the true capsule.
The venous plexus lies deep to the true capsule, so it stays dry.
The recurrent nerve is outside.
Not the reason.

title: Why is lumbar puncture done below L3?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Why is lumbar puncture done below L3?
body.explanation: In adults the cord ends at L1/L2. Below it, only the cauda equina floats in CSF, and the roots move aside from the needle.
option_notes: Not the reason.
The cord ends at L1/L2, so a needle below L3 meets only roots.
CSF is made in the ventricles.
The sac ends at S2.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the pyramid. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: This is at the arrow: the ridge on the front of the medulla carrying corticospinal fibres.
Not at the arrow; this is the nerves at the angle between pons, medulla and cerebellum.
Not at the arrow; this is the bulging middle part of the brainstem.
Not at the arrow; this is the large nerve from the side of the pons.

title: What proportion of the canal is cartilaginous?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What proportion of the canal is cartilaginous?
body.explanation: The cartilaginous part forms the outer third (8 mm); the bony part forms the inner two thirds (16 mm).
option_notes: The outer third is cartilage, the inner two thirds bone.
The inner part is bone.
Only one third is cartilage.
Most of the canal is bone.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the optic chiasm. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which structure links the nervous system to the endocrine system through the pituitary?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure links the nervous system to the endocrine system through the pituitary?
body.explanation: The hypothalamus ends in the infundibulum connected to the pituitary; it is the interface between nervous and endocrine systems.
option_notes: The hypothalamus controls the pituitary gland.
The thalamus is a sensory relay.
The pineal secretes melatonin but does not control the pituitary.
The subthalamic nucleus is a motor structure.

title: Which cranial nerve controls the muscles of mastication?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cranial nerve controls the muscles of mastication?
body.explanation: CN V is mixed: sensation of the face and motor to the muscles of mastication. CN VII moves the muscles of facial expression.

title: Into which two triangles is the posterior triangle subdivided?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Into which two triangles is the posterior triangle subdivided?
body.explanation: The posterior triangle is subdivided into the occipital triangle and the subclavian, or omoclavicular, triangle.

title: What is the average size of a frontal sinus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the average size of a frontal sinus?
body.explanation: There is one frontal sinus on each side. They are variable in size and are the most superior of the sinuses, with an average size of 2.5 cm, and each is triangular in shape.

title: What do the pyramidal tracts control?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What do the pyramidal tracts control?
body.explanation: Pyramidal tracts control voluntary movement of the body and face; extrapyramidal tracts control involuntary, automatic activity such as tone, balance, posture and locomotion.

title: Which are the three parts of the brainstem, from top to bottom?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are the three parts of the brainstem, from top to bottom?
body.explanation: The brainstem has three sections in descending order: midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata.
option_notes: Correct order from above down.
This is bottom to top.
The thalamus is diencephalon.
The midbrain is above the pons.

title: Which tract is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which tract is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Gracile fasciculus: the medial part of the dorsal column: fine touch and position sense from the lower body.
option_notes: Posterior spinocerebellar tract is unconscious proprioception to the cerebellum, at the edge of the lateral funiculus.
The medial part of the dorsal column: fine touch and position sense from the lower body.
Lateral corticospinal tract is the main crossed motor tract, in the lateral funiculus.
Lateral spinothalamic tract is pain and temperature, in the lateral funiculus.

title: Around which cavity is the diencephalon organised?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Around which cavity is the diencephalon organised?
body.explanation: The diencephalon is the central brain around the third ventricle, above the brainstem and below the corpus callosum and cortex.
option_notes: The fourth ventricle belongs to the hindbrain.
The diencephalon surrounds the third ventricle.
Those are in the hemispheres.
The aqueduct is in the midbrain.

title: Where is the insula?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where is the insula?
body.explanation: The insular lobe is folded deep within the lateral sulcus and divided into two lobules: an anterior with 3 convolutions and a posterior with 2.
option_notes: Not on the medial face.
Not there.
Not there.
Deep in the lateral sulcus, hidden by the opercula.

title: Which photoreceptors are responsible for vision at low light levels?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which photoreceptors are responsible for vision at low light levels?
body.explanation: Rods handle scotopic (low light) vision, do not mediate colour vision and have low spatial acuity. Cones work at higher light levels (photopic vision), give colour vision and high spatial acuity. The central fovea is populated exclusively by cones.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Subarachnoid space. Between arachnoid and pia; holds most of the CSF and widens into cisterns.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the tufts pushing into the sinus that absorb CSF.
Not at the arrow; this is the openings from each lateral ventricle into the third ventricle.
Not at the arrow; this is the paired C-shaped cavities in the hemispheres.
This is at the arrow: the CSF-filled space around the brain and cord.

title: What are the contents of Farabeuf's triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What are the contents of Farabeuf's triangle?
options: The carotid bifurcation and a node
The lingual artery and hypoglossal nerve
The submandibular gland and facial vein
The accessory nerve and cervical plexus
body.explanation: Its contents are one branch of the common carotid artery, or the carotid bifurcation, and the jugulodigastric lymph node. It is a well-known sign for identifying the common carotid artery and its bifurcation.

title: What lies behind the medial side of the lateral lobes?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What lies behind the medial side of the lateral lobes?
body.explanation: Backwards, the medial side of the lateral lobes responds to the pharynx and then to the oesophagus.
option_notes: The pharynx and oesophagus lie behind its medial side.
The carotid sheath lies posterolaterally.
These lie further back.
Not only them.

title: Which part of the thalamus relays hearing to the auditory cortex?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which part of the thalamus relays hearing to the auditory cortex?
body.explanation: The medial geniculate body receives auditory input from the inferior colliculus and sends it to the temporal auditory cortex.
option_notes: MGB: hearing (M for music).
The LGB relays vision.
The pulvinar is the posterior thalamus.
The anterior nucleus is limbic.

title: Which tract is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which tract is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Posterior spinocerebellar tract: unconscious proprioception to the cerebellum, at the edge of the lateral funiculus.
option_notes: Unconscious proprioception to the cerebellum, at the edge of the lateral funiculus.
Cuneate fasciculus is the lateral part of the dorsal column: fine touch and position sense from the upper body.
Lateral spinothalamic tract is pain and temperature, in the lateral funiculus.
Gracile fasciculus is the medial part of the dorsal column: fine touch and position sense from the lower body.

title: Initially, what separates the nasal cavity from the primary oral cavity?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Initially, what separates the nasal cavity from the primary oral cavity?
body.explanation: Initially the oronasal membrane separates the two. The nasal cavity is later separated from the oral cavity by the maturation of the primary and secondary palate.

title: Which vessels drain the orbit? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which vessels drain the orbit? (choose all)
body.explanation: The superior and inferior ophthalmic veins and the vortex veins drain the orbit. The central retinal and lacrimal arteries are part of the arterial supply.

title: What anchors the spinal cord to the coccyx?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What anchors the spinal cord to the coccyx?
body.explanation: The filum terminale extends from the tip of the conus medullaris to the first coccygeal vertebra, anchoring the cord.
option_notes: Fixes the cord sideways to the dura.
The cone-shaped end of the cord.
The filum terminale ends on the coccyx.
Lies on the vertebral bodies.

title: Which gyrus is the primary motor area?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus is the primary motor area?
body.explanation: The precentral gyrus of the frontal lobe is the motor strip; the postcentral gyrus of the parietal lobe is the sensory strip.
option_notes: The postcentral gyrus is sensory.
Auditory.
Limbic.
The precentral gyrus is primary motor.

title: Which nerves supply the external ear?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerves supply the external ear?
body.explanation: The external ear is supplied by the superficial cervical plexus, the nervus intermedius (VII bis) and the trigeminal nerve.
option_notes: Great auricular and lesser occipital nerves (cervical plexus).
The auriculotemporal nerve is a V3 branch.
The optic nerve serves vision.
XII supplies the tongue.

title: What is the most essential content of the orbit?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the most essential content of the orbit?
body.explanation: The lecture lists the orbital contents as the eyeball (the most essential), the extraocular muscles, fascia bulbi, nerves, vessels, the ciliary ganglion, the lacrimal gland and orbital fat.

title: Which muscle draws down the medial angle of the eyebrows and produces transverse wrinkles over the bridge of the nose?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscle draws down the medial angle of the eyebrows and produces transverse wrinkles over the bridge of the nose?
body.explanation: The procerus is a small pyramidal slip arising from the nasal bone and upper part of the lateral nasal cartilage, inserting into the skin of the lower forehead between the eyebrows.

title: From which roots does the brachial plexus form?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: From which roots does the brachial plexus form?
body.explanation: The brachial plexus (C4 to T1) gives the radial, axillary, ulnar and median nerves of the arm.

title: Where does the corticospinal tract mainly cross?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the corticospinal tract mainly cross?
body.explanation: It starts mainly in the primary motor cortex, passes through the internal capsule and cerebral peduncles, and most fibres decussate in the medulla.
option_notes: It passes through, not crosses.
Most fibres cross in the medullary pyramids.
It descends there uncrossed.
It starts there.

title: At which vertebral levels does the thyroid lie?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: At which vertebral levels does the thyroid lie?
body.explanation: The gland lies in the lower part of the front and side of the neck, opposite the C5, C6, C7 and T1 vertebrae, clasping the upper part of the trachea.
option_notes: Too high.
The thyroid lies at C5 to T1.
Too high; this is the larynx level.
Too low.

title: Which structures bound the spinal canal laterally?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structures bound the spinal canal laterally?
body.explanation: Anteriorly the vertebral bodies, discs and longitudinal ligaments; posteriorly the laminae; laterally the pedicles, which delimit the intervertebral foramina.
option_notes: Back wall.
Front wall.
The pedicles form the sides.
Behind.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the brachial plexus (c4 to t1). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Where is the lacrimal gland located?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where is the lacrimal gland located?
options: In the lacrimal fossa on the medial wall
In the lacrimal fossa, superolateral in the orbit
Behind the inferior oblique, in the floor
Within the tarsal plate of the upper eyelid, at the margin
body.explanation: The lacrimal gland sits anteriorly in the superolateral aspect of the orbit, within the lacrimal fossa, a depression in the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the sclera. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: A rare cause of hydrocephalus by overproduction of CSF is:
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: A rare cause of hydrocephalus by overproduction of CSF is:
body.explanation: The others impair flow or absorption.
option_notes: Obstruction.
Poor absorption.
Papillomas overproduce CSF.
Poor absorption.

title: Where does the sciatic nerve leave the pelvis?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the sciatic nerve leave the pelvis?
body.explanation: The largest and longest nerve, from L4 to S3, it exits through the greater sciatic foramen, usually below piriformis.

title: Where are the ceruminous glands of the canal?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where are the ceruminous glands of the canal?
