body.explanation: The orbital floor (maxilla, zygomatic, palatine) separates the orbit from the maxillary sinus below. The frontal sinus lies above, the ethmoidal cells medially.

title: Which ventricle lies between the two thalami?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which ventricle lies between the two thalami?
body.explanation: The third ventricle is a median cleft between the two thalami.
option_notes: Between the thalami.
Behind the pons and medulla.
In each hemisphere.
Not a ventricle of the system.

title: Which part of the nervous system controls involuntary functions such as heart rate and digestion?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which part of the nervous system controls involuntary functions such as heart rate and digestion?
body.explanation: The autonomic system responds automatically to internal and external changes; the somatic system controls voluntary actions.
option_notes: Autonomic: automatic, involuntary control.
Somatic: voluntary actions.
The cerebellum coordinates movement.
These are sensory ganglia.

title: Which nerve passes through the superior orbital fissure OUTSIDE the common tendinous ring?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerve passes through the superior orbital fissure OUTSIDE the common tendinous ring?
options: Inferior division of the oculomotor nerve
body.explanation: Outside the ring: lacrimal nerve, frontal nerve, trochlear nerve (CN IV) and the superior ophthalmic vein (LFT + vein). Inside the ring: both divisions of CN III, CN VI and the nasociliary nerve.

title: What is the main function of the basal ganglia?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the main function of the basal ganglia?
body.explanation: They receive movement plans from the cortex, adjust them and send instructions via the thalamus back to the cortex, then down the pyramidal tracts.
option_notes: They fine-tune and control movement.
Choroid plexuses make CSF.
The thalamus relays vision.
The brainstem controls breathing.

title: What is retinal detachment?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is retinal detachment?
body.explanation: Retinal detachment is an emergency in which a thin layer of tissue at the back of the eye pulls away from the layer of blood vessels that provides it with oxygen and nutrients. It is often accompanied by flashes and floaters.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the temporomandibular joint. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: At what angle do the semicircular canals lie to each other?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: At what angle do the semicircular canals lie to each other?
body.explanation: There are three bony semicircular canals, anterior, posterior and lateral, lying in three planes at 90 degrees to each other.
option_notes: Not 45.
Not 60.
They are not in one plane.
Each canal is at right angles to the others.

title: Which treatments for retinal detachment does the lecture mention? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which treatments for retinal detachment does the lecture mention? (choose all)
body.explanation: The lecture lists removing and replacing the jelly inside the eye (vitrectomy), attaching a small band around the eye to push the wall and retina closer together (scleral buckling), and injecting a bubble of gas to push the retina back (pneumatic retinopexy).

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Fornix: the arched fibre tract from the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies.
option_notes: Globus pallidus is the inner part of the lentiform nucleus, medial to the putamen.
Hippocampus is the curved structure in the floor of the temporal horn: memory.
The arched fibre tract from the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies.
Putamen is the outer part of the lentiform nucleus.

title: Which part of the temporal bone houses most of the ear?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which part of the temporal bone houses most of the ear?
options: The zygomatic process of the bone
body.explanation: The ear is divided into external, middle and inner parts, mostly within the petrous part of the temporal bone.
option_notes: The petrous part holds the middle and inner ear.
The squamous part is the flat side wall of the skull.
The mastoid lies behind; it holds air cells, not the ear itself.
The zygomatic process forms part of the cheek arch.

title: Which arteries supply the pharynx? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which arteries supply the pharynx? (choose all)
body.explanation: The pharynx is supplied by the ascending pharyngeal artery (external carotid), the ascending palatine and tonsillar arteries (facial), the greater palatine and pharyngeal arteries (maxillary) and the lingual artery.
option_notes: Correct: from the external carotid, the main supply of the pharynx.
Correct: a branch of the facial artery in the neck.
Wrong: a terminal branch of the external carotid supplying the scalp and temple.
Wrong: supplies the back of the scalp, not the pharynx.

title: Which nerve carries general sensation from the anterior two thirds of the tongue?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerve carries general sensation from the anterior two thirds of the tongue?
options: The chorda tympani, from CN VII
The internal laryngeal nerve, from CN X
body.explanation: Anterior two thirds: general sensation by the lingual nerve (a branch of CN V3), special sensation (taste) by the chorda tympani (CN VII). Posterior third: general and special sensation by the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX). Base: general and special sensation by the internal laryngeal nerve (CN X).

title: Which cartilage is the only complete ring in the airway?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cartilage is the only complete ring in the airway?
body.explanation: The cricoid is a signet-shaped ring with a narrow anterior arch and a broad posterior lamina, at the level of C6. It completely encircles the lumen of the larynx and is considered the foundation stone of the larynx.
option_notes: The thyroid is open behind.
The cricoid is the only complete ring.
The epiglottis is a leaf.
The arytenoid is a pyramid.

title: What separates the anterior two thirds from the posterior third of the tongue?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What separates the anterior two thirds from the posterior third of the tongue?
options: The median septum of the tongue
body.explanation: The dorsal surface is divided into anterior two thirds and posterior one third by a V-shaped sulcus terminalis. The apex of the sulcus faces backward and is marked by a pit called the foramen cecum.

title: Which cavity runs through the midbrain?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cavity runs through the midbrain?
options: The central canal of the cord
body.explanation: Your professor's question: the aqueduct of Sylvius runs through the midbrain; the fourth ventricle lies behind the pons and medulla.
option_notes: The cerebral aqueduct.
Pons and medulla.
Diencephalon.
Spinal cord.

title: Which is the main source of corticospinal fibres?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which is the main source of corticospinal fibres?
body.explanation: Inputs come from the primary motor cortex (the main one), the premotor cortex and the supplementary motor area.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the incus. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is air spaces in the mastoid behind the middle ear.
This is at the arrow: the middle ossicle, between malleus and stapes.
Not at the arrow; this is the air space behind the eardrum holding the ossicles.
Not at the arrow; this is the outer ossicle, its handle attached to the eardrum.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the optic chiasm. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Postcentral gyrus: the gyrus just behind the central sulcus: the primary somatosensory cortex.
option_notes: Transverse temporal gyri (Heschl) is the gyri on the upper surface of the temporal lobe, inside the lateral sulcus: the primary auditory cortex.
The gyrus just behind the central sulcus: the primary somatosensory cortex.
Inferior temporal gyrus is the lowest gyrus of the lateral temporal lobe.
Fusiform (lateral occipitotemporal) gyrus is the gyrus on the inferior surface between the inferior temporal and parahippocampal gyri.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the retina (both eyes). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which part of the neuron carries impulses away from the cell body?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which part of the neuron carries impulses away from the cell body?
body.explanation: Dendrites receive incoming signals; the axon transmits electrical impulses away from the soma.
option_notes: The axon carries impulses away.
Dendrites receive signals.
The soma holds the nucleus.
The nucleus is inside the soma.

title: The fourth ventricle opens into the subarachnoid space through:
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The fourth ventricle opens into the subarachnoid space through:
options: The central canal of the spinal cord
The aqueduct of Sylvius in the midbrain
The foramina of Luschka and Magendie
body.explanation: One median (Magendie) and two lateral (Luschka) apertures.
option_notes: Monro is between lateral and third ventricles.
It continues downward, not out.
It enters the fourth ventricle.
Luschka (lateral) and Magendie (median) apertures.

title: Which three types of papillae are on the anterior two thirds of the tongue?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which three types of papillae are on the anterior two thirds of the tongue?
body.explanation: The mucosa of the anterior two thirds is rough and shows three types of papillae: filiform, fungiform and vallate. The posterior third has no papillae but shows a nodular surface because of underlying lymphatic nodules, the lingual tonsils.

title: Which nerve nuclei receive corticobulbar fibres for eye movement?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerve nuclei receive corticobulbar fibres for eye movement?
body.explanation: One group ends in the oculomotor, trochlear and abducens nuclei; others in the motor nuclei of V, VII, IX, X and XI.

title: What opens into the superior meatus? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What opens into the superior meatus? (choose all)
body.explanation: Superior meatus: the posterior ethmoidal cells, the sphenoidal sinus and the sphenopalatine foramen. The frontal sinus drains into the middle meatus and the nasolacrimal duct into the inferior meatus.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
options: Opercular part of the inferior frontal gyrus
body.explanation: Opercular part of the inferior frontal gyrus: the back part of the inferior frontal gyrus; with the triangular part it forms Broca's area (dominant side).
option_notes: Middle frontal gyrus is the middle horizontal gyrus of the lateral frontal lobe.
Postcentral gyrus is the gyrus just behind the central sulcus: the primary somatosensory cortex.
Superior temporal gyrus is the top gyrus of the temporal lobe, under the lateral sulcus; its back part holds Wernicke's area.
The back part of the inferior frontal gyrus; with the triangular part it forms Broca's area (dominant side).

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Parahippocampal gyrus: the medial temporal gyrus on the inferior surface, ending in front in the uncus.
option_notes: Cuneus is the wedge of medial occipital cortex between the calcarine and parieto-occipital sulci.
Cingulate gyrus is the gyrus arching around the corpus callosum on the medial surface (limbic lobe).
Insula is the cortex hidden deep in the lateral sulcus, covered by the opercula.
The medial temporal gyrus on the inferior surface, ending in front in the uncus.

title: What lies beneath the floor of the tympanic cavity?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What lies beneath the floor of the tympanic cavity?
body.explanation: The floor is a thin plate of bone separating the cavity from the jugular bulb. Sometimes it is congenitally deficient and the bulb projects into the middle ear, covered only by mucosa.
option_notes: The carotid lies in front.
That is above the roof.
The jugular bulb lies under the floor.
The antrum lies behind.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Vermis: the midline part of the cerebellum joining the two hemispheres.
option_notes: Superior cerebellar peduncle is the bundle joining the cerebellum to the midbrain; the main cerebellar output.
The midline part of the cerebellum joining the two hemispheres.
Cerebellar tonsil is the rounded part of the inferior hemisphere beside the vermis, above the foramen magnum.
Flocculus is the small lobule beside the middle cerebellar peduncle, part of the flocculonodular lobe.

title: Which glial cells form part of the blood-brain barrier?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which glial cells form part of the blood-brain barrier?
body.explanation: Astrocytes give structural support, regulate ion balance and form part of the blood-brain barrier.
option_notes: Astrocytes.
Immune cells.
PNS myelin.
PNS ganglia.

title: Which cells secrete calcitonin, and what does it do?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cells secrete calcitonin, and what does it do?
options: The follicular cells; it is hypercalcemic
The C cells; it is hypocalcemic
The parathyroid chief cells; it lowers phosphate
The C cells; it raises blood calcium
body.explanation: Calcitonin is secreted by the C cells. It is a hypocalcemic hormone that inhibits bone demineralization, preventing the passage of calcium into the blood, and is regulated by the level of calcium in the blood.
option_notes: Follicular cells make T3/T4, and calcitonin lowers calcium.
C cells secrete calcitonin, which lowers calcium.
Parathyroids make PTH.
Calcitonin lowers calcium.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Cerebral peduncle (crus cerebri): the thick pillar on the front of the midbrain carrying descending fibres.
option_notes: Medulla oblongata is the lowest part of the brainstem, continuous with the spinal cord.
The thick pillar on the front of the midbrain carrying descending fibres.
Superior colliculus is the upper pair of bumps on the back of the midbrain: visual reflexes.
Inferior colliculus is the lower pair of bumps on the back of the midbrain: auditory pathway.

title: Which is the smallest of the major salivary glands?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which is the smallest of the major salivary glands?
options: They are all the same size
body.explanation: The sublingual gland is the smallest of the major salivary glands. It lies between the floor of the mouth, below the mucosa and above the mylohyoid muscle. It is a mixed gland, but mucous units predominate.

title: Which structure is a neurostimulation target in Parkinson's disease?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is a neurostimulation target in Parkinson's disease?
body.explanation: The subthalamic nucleus (Luys' body), at the junction of diencephalon and midbrain, is a deep brain stimulation target.
option_notes: Not the usual target.
Not a target.
The subthalamic nucleus is a deep brain stimulation target.
Not a target.

title: By how many openings do the semicircular canals open into the vestibule?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: By how many openings do the semicircular canals open into the vestibule?
body.explanation: Three canals would give six ends, but the anterior and posterior canals share the crus commune, so there are five openings.
option_notes: More than three.
Six ends, but two share the crus commune: five openings.
Two ends are shared.
One more.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the lumbar plexus (femoral nerve). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which capsule is formed by condensation of the gland's own fibrous stroma?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which capsule is formed by condensation of the gland's own fibrous stroma?
body.explanation: The gland is covered by two capsules: an inner true capsule, formed by peripheral condensation of the fibrous stroma of the gland, and an outer false capsule derived from the splitting of the pretracheal fascia.
option_notes: The true capsule is the gland's own condensed stroma.
The false capsule comes from pretracheal fascia.
That forms the false capsule.
The carotid sheath surrounds the vessels.

title: Which flexure is the most prominent, located at the level of the midbrain?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which flexure is the most prominent, located at the level of the midbrain?
body.explanation: The cephalic flexure, at the midbrain, gives the brain its forward bend on the brainstem.
option_notes: The cephalic flexure.
Between hindbrain and spinal cord.
Between metencephalon and myelencephalon.
Not an embryonic brain flexure.

title: Which features belong to the nasopharynx? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which features belong to the nasopharynx? (choose all)
body.explanation: Nasopharynx: pharyngeal tonsil (adenoids), the auditory tube opening and the torus tubarius. The palatine tonsil is in the oropharynx and the piriform recess in the laryngopharynx.

title: Where does the sympathetic outflow originate?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the sympathetic outflow originate?
options: The brainstem and S2 to S4
The lateral horn of T1 to L2
The ventral horn of C1 to C8
body.explanation: Sympathetic: thoracolumbar, from the lateral horn of T1 to L2. Parasympathetic: craniosacral, from brainstem nuclei (III, VII, IX, X) and S2 to S4.

title: Which lobe controls personality, judgment and planning?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which lobe controls personality, judgment and planning?
body.explanation: The frontal lobe controls personality, behaviour, emotions, judgment and planning.
option_notes: Frontal lobe damage changes personality and judgment.
The occipital lobe is for vision.
The temporal lobe is for hearing and memory.
The insula handles taste, visceral sensation and autonomic control.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the central sulcus (rolando). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: This is at the arrow: the groove between frontal and parietal lobes.
Not at the arrow; this is the gyrus behind the central sulcus.
Not at the arrow; this is the back of the superior temporal gyrus.
Not at the arrow; this is the lobe in front of the central sulcus.

title: Which neurotransmitter do the basal ganglia need to function?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which neurotransmitter do the basal ganglia need to function?
body.explanation: Their proper functioning requires dopamine released at the input nuclei, which is why its loss causes Parkinson's disease.
option_notes: Dopamine (from the substantia nigra).
Not the key one.
Not the key one.
Glycine acts in the cord.

title: Which structure forms the medial boundary of the internal capsule?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure forms the medial boundary of the internal capsule?
options: The thalamus and the head of the caudate nucleus
body.explanation: The internal capsule lies between the thalamus and caudate medially and the lentiform nucleus laterally.
option_notes: These lie medial to the internal capsule.
The lentiform nucleus is lateral to it.
The claustrum lies beside the external capsule.
The insula is cortex, further out.

title: Which part of the eyelid carries the eyelashes?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which part of the eyelid carries the eyelashes?
options: The medial part of the eyelid, next to the nose
The lateral part, the ciliary part
body.explanation: The eyelid has a medial part and a lateral part. The lateral part carries the eyelashes and is known as the ciliary part.

title: Which epithelium covers the vocal cords?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which epithelium covers the vocal cords?
body.explanation: The laryngeal epithelium is respiratory type (cylindric stratified) throughout, except at the vocal cords and the upper half of the epiglottis, which are non-keratinized stratified squamous.
option_notes: Lines the rest of the larynx.
Not here.
Not keratinised.
Non-keratinised stratified squamous resists friction.

title: Which bones meet at the pterion?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which bones meet at the pterion?
options: Frontal, parietal, occipital and lesser wing of the sphenoid
Frontal, nasal, maxilla and zygomatic bone together
Parietal, occipital, squamous temporal and the mastoid process of the temporal bone
Frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and greater wing of sphenoid
body.explanation: The pterion is the H-shaped junction of the frontal bone, parietal bone, squamous part of the temporal bone and greater wing of the sphenoid. It lies over the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery.

title: What does the medial wall of each thalamus form?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the medial wall of each thalamus form?
options: The floor of the lateral ventricle
The roof of the fourth ventricle
Side wall of the third ventricle
body.explanation: The medial surfaces of the two thalami form the lateral walls of the third ventricle.
option_notes: Not the floor.
Not the fourth ventricle.
Not this.
It forms the side wall of the third ventricle.

title: Which embryonic vesicles form the brainstem?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which embryonic vesicles form the brainstem?
body.explanation: The brainstem comes from the mesencephalon (3rd), metencephalon (4th) and myelencephalon (5th vesicles).
option_notes: Midbrain, pons and medulla come from these.
These form the cerebrum.
The forebrain forms the cerebrum and diencephalon.
The telencephalon forms the hemispheres.

title: How many pairs of spinal nerves are there?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How many pairs of spinal nerves are there?
body.explanation: There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves and 31 pairs of spinal nerves.
option_notes: 31 pairs of spinal nerves.
12 is the number of cranial nerve pairs.
33 is the number of vertebrae.
8 is the number of cervical nerve pairs.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the frontal lobe. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: This is at the arrow: the lobe in front of the central sulcus.
Not at the arrow; this is the deep groove separating the temporal lobe from the frontal and parietal lobes.
Not at the arrow; this is the back of the superior temporal gyrus.
Not at the arrow; this is the gyrus behind the central sulcus.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the pons (fibres split into fascicles). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: What forms the floor of the oral cavity proper?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the floor of the oral cavity proper?
body.explanation: The oral cavity proper is the cavity within the alveolar margins of the maxillae and the mandible. Its roof is the hard palate anteriorly and the soft palate posteriorly; its floor is formed by the mylohyoid muscle, and the anterior two thirds of the tongue lies on that floor.

title: Which lobe is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which lobe is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Frontal lobe: in front of the central sulcus and above the lateral sulcus.
option_notes: The parietal lobe lies behind the central sulcus, above the lateral sulcus, in front of the parieto-occipital sulcus.
The temporal lobe lies below the lateral sulcus.
The frontal lobe lies in front of the central sulcus and above the lateral sulcus.
The occipital lobe lies at the back, behind the parieto-occipital sulcus.

title: Which structures does the visual pathway pass through between the eye and the cortex? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structures does the visual pathway pass through between the eye and the cortex? (choose all)
body.explanation: The pathway runs eye, optic nerve, optic chiasm, optic tract, lateral geniculate nucleus, optic radiation, primary visual cortex. The ciliary ganglion belongs to the pupillary pathway and the trochlea to the superior oblique.

title: Which functional division is most associated with balance and eye movements?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which functional division is most associated with balance and eye movements?
body.explanation: The vestibulocerebellum (flocculonodular lobe) controls equilibrium, balance and coordinated eye movements.
option_notes: Balance and eye movements.
Tone, posture, trunk and limb coordination.
Planning and timing of skilled movements.
The dentate belongs to the cerebrocerebellum.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the hard palate. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: What does the peripheral nervous system include?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the peripheral nervous system include?
body.explanation: The PNS comprises all neural structures outside the brain and spinal cord: cranial nerves, spinal nerves, and their branches, plexuses and ganglia.

title: What is the epislera?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the epislera?
options: The innermost layer of the choroid
The outermost layer of the sclera
The transparent front of the outer coat
A ring of muscle inside the iris
body.explanation: The episclera is the outermost layer of the sclera, composed of loose fibrous elastic tissue, and attaches to Tenon's capsule. A vascular plexus of superficial and deep episcleral vessels lies between the bulbar conjunctiva and the sclera.

title: Where is the cerebellum located?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where is the cerebellum located?
body.explanation: The cerebellum lies in the posterior cranial fossa, under the tentorium, behind the pons and medulla.
option_notes: It lies in the posterior fossa behind the brainstem.
That holds the frontal lobes.
That holds the temporal lobes.
The ventricles hold CSF, not brain parts.

title: What is the vestibule of the mouth?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the vestibule of the mouth?
options: The space behind the last molar tooth
The cavity within the alveolar margins
The space between cheeks and gums
body.explanation: The vestibule is a slit-like space between the cheeks and the gums, communicating with the exterior through the oral fissure. When the jaws are closed it communicates with the oral cavity proper behind the third molar tooth on each side.

title: Why is the optic nerve surrounded by CSF?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Why is the optic nerve surrounded by CSF?
options: Because it runs inside a bony canal full of fluid
Because it is a peripheral nerve with a synovial sheath
Because it is wrapped in the meninges
Because it passes through the cavernous sinus
body.explanation: The optic nerve is sheathed by dura, arachnoid and pia, with a subarachnoid space containing CSF. Raised intracranial pressure is therefore transmitted along the nerve.

title: Where does the submandibular duct open?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the submandibular duct open?
options: Into the floor of the nose
body.explanation: The main excretory duct of the submandibular gland is Wharton's duct. It runs forward above the mylohyoid muscle, lying just below the mucosa and the floor of the mouth, and opens on the sublingual papilla, lateral to the lingual frenulum.

title: What is the terminal branch of the facial artery called?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the terminal branch of the facial artery called?
body.explanation: After giving the labial branches, the facial artery ascends along the side of the nose in the nasolabial fold and ends as the angular artery, supplying the external nose, lower eyelid, orbicularis oculi and lacrimal sac.

title: What is the front end of the corpus callosum called?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the front end of the corpus callosum called?
body.explanation: In front is the genu, ending in the beak or rostrum; behind is the splenium.
option_notes: The splenium is the back end.
The fornix is below it.
The genu is the front bend.
The uncus is temporal.

title: What is the sensory receptor for hearing?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the sensory receptor for hearing?
options: The cristae ampullaris of the ducts
body.explanation: The organ of Corti in the cochlear duct is the receptor for hearing. The maculae of the saccule and utricle serve static balance; the cristae ampullaris of the semicircular ducts serve kinetic balance.
option_notes: Maculae serve balance.
Cristae serve balance.
The stria makes endolymph.
The organ of Corti is the hearing receptor.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the orbicularis oculi. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the trachea. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the large shield-shaped cartilage of the larynx (Adam's apple).
Not at the arrow; this is the thyrocervical trunk branch reaching the lower lobe.
This is at the arrow: the tube of C-shaped rings below the cricoid.
Not at the arrow; this is the lateral lobe on the patient's right (viewer's left).

title: What forms the floor of Lesser's triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the floor of Lesser's triangle?
body.explanation: The floor of Lesser's triangle is formed by the hyoglossus and mylohyoid muscles.

title: Which vein provides the main venous drainage of the orbit?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which vein provides the main venous drainage of the orbit?
body.explanation: The superior ophthalmic vein originates in the superonasal quadrant of the orbit and extends posteriorly through the medial part of the superior orbital fissure into the cavernous sinus.

title: What is the sixth occipital gyrus called?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the sixth occipital gyrus called?
body.explanation: The occipital lobe has six gyri; the sixth, on the internal face, is the cuneus.
option_notes: The uncus is temporal.
The insula is hidden in the lateral sulcus.
The cuneus is O6.
The precuneus is parietal.

title: What connects the brainstem to the cerebellum?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What connects the brainstem to the cerebellum?
body.explanation: Superior peduncle to the midbrain, middle to the pons, inferior to the medulla. Above, the transverse fissure of Bichat joins the diencephalon; below, the foramen magnum leads to the cord.
option_notes: The opening into the spinal canal.
Three pairs of peduncles.
Not this.
These join colliculi to geniculate bodies.

title: The facial vein begins at the medial angle of the eye as the continuation of which vein?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The facial vein begins at the medial angle of the eye as the continuation of which vein?
body.explanation: The supratrochlear and supraorbital veins merge at the medial angle of the eye to form the angular vein, which becomes the facial vein as it descends the face.

title: Which neurotransmitter is lacking in Parkinson's disease, disturbing the basal ganglia?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which neurotransmitter is lacking in Parkinson's disease, disturbing the basal ganglia?
body.explanation: The basal ganglia need dopamine released at their input nuclei to work properly.
option_notes: Loss of dopamine-producing neurons causes Parkinson's disease.
Acetylcholine is not the missing transmitter.
Glycine acts mainly in the spinal cord.
Histamine is not the cause.

title: What bounds the carotid triangle above?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What bounds the carotid triangle above?
body.explanation: The carotid triangle is bounded below and anteroinferiorly by the superior belly of omohyoid, above by stylohyoid and the posterior belly of digastric, and posteriorly by sternocleidomastoid.

title: Which plexus gives the phrenic nerve?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which plexus gives the phrenic nerve?
body.explanation: The cervical plexus (C1 to C5) supplies the posterior neck and head and gives the phrenic nerve to the diaphragm.

title: From which germ layer does the nervous system derive?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: From which germ layer does the nervous system derive?
body.explanation: The whole nervous system derives from ectoderm, except its blood vessels and some neurological elements.
option_notes: Ectoderm.
Mesoderm gives its blood vessels.
Endoderm gives the gut lining.
The neural crest itself comes from ectoderm.

title: Which sinuses open into the middle meatus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which sinuses open into the middle meatus?
options: Posterior ethmoidal cells and the sphenoidal sinus
body.explanation: Middle meatus: the anterior ethmoidal cells, the ostium of the maxillary sinus and the frontal sinus. Superior meatus: the posterior ethmoidal cells, the sphenoidal sinus and the sphenopalatine foramen.

title: Where do the inferior thyroid veins drain?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where do the inferior thyroid veins drain?
options: Into the superior vena cava directly
body.explanation: The superior thyroid vein drains into the internal jugular vein, most often via the thyro-linguo-facial (Farabeuf) trunk. The middle thyroid veins join the internal jugular directly. The inferior thyroid veins descend to the left brachiocephalic vein.
option_notes: The superior and middle veins drain there.
Not the subclavian.
Not directly.
Into the left brachiocephalic vein.

title: Name the four extrinsic muscles of the tongue.
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Name the four extrinsic muscles of the tongue.
options: Tensor and levator veli palatini and the two pterygoids
body.explanation: The extrinsic muscles connect the tongue to the soft palate and the bones (mandible, hyoid bone, styloid process): palatoglossus, genioglossus, hyoglossus and styloglossus.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the zygomatic. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which bones are shown as part of the cranial base in the lecture figure? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which bones are shown as part of the cranial base in the lecture figure? (choose all)
body.explanation: The lecture's cranial base figure colours the frontal, sphenoid, temporal, parietal, occipital and ethmoid bones. The nasal bone and vomer are facial bones that take no part in the cranial base.

title: Which tract supplies the head and neck muscles?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which tract supplies the head and neck muscles?
body.explanation: Corticospinal tracts supply the body; corticobulbar tracts supply the head and neck through the cranial nerve motor nuclei.

title: Which structures pass through the superior orbital fissure INSIDE the common tendinous ring? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structures pass through the superior orbital fissure INSIDE the common tendinous ring? (choose all)
body.explanation: Inside the ring: both divisions of CN III, CN VI and the nasociliary nerve. The frontal nerve and the superior ophthalmic vein pass outside the ring.

title: A patient walks with an unsteady, staggering gait and keeps losing balance, but limb coordination is normal when lying down. Which part is most likely damaged?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: A patient walks with an unsteady, staggering gait and keeps losing balance, but limb coordination is normal when lying down. Which part is most likely damaged?
body.explanation: Damage to the flocculonodular lobe causes loss of equilibrium with an altered walking gait.
option_notes: Loss of equilibrium points to the vestibulocerebellum.
Lateral damage disturbs skilled limb movements.
The dentate serves the lateral hemisphere.
Peduncle lesions are not the classic cause here.

title: Which nerve supplies the levator palpebrae superioris?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerve supplies the levator palpebrae superioris?
options: Abducens nerve (CN VI), as for the lateral rectus
body.explanation: The levator palpebrae superioris raises the upper eyelid and is supplied by CN III. Its smooth part, the superior tarsal muscle, is supplied by sympathetic fibres.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Cingulate gyrus: the gyrus arching around the corpus callosum on the medial surface (limbic lobe).
option_notes: Parahippocampal gyrus is the medial temporal gyrus on the inferior surface, ending in front in the uncus.
Transverse temporal gyri (Heschl) is the gyri on the upper surface of the temporal lobe, inside the lateral sulcus: the primary auditory cortex.
The gyrus arching around the corpus callosum on the medial surface (limbic lobe).
Precentral gyrus is the gyrus just in front of the central sulcus: the primary motor cortex.

title: What does the anterior corticospinal tract supply?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the anterior corticospinal tract supply?
body.explanation: It descends ipsilaterally, crosses at the segmental level and ends in the ventral horn of cervical and upper thoracic segments, supplying the axial muscles.

title: Name the three parts of the near response.
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Name the three parts of the near response.
options: Pupil dilation, lid elevation and convergence
Lens flattening, pupil dilation and divergence
body.explanation: The lecture gives four linked boxes: lens changes (accommodation), changes in the pupil, the near response and convergence of the eyes. Its goal is clear vision of a nearby object.

title: Which artery supplying the septum is a branch of the facial artery?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which artery supplying the septum is a branch of the facial artery?
body.explanation: The septum is supplied by septal branches of the anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteries (from the ophthalmic), the sphenopalatine and greater palatine arteries (from the maxillary), and the superior labial artery (from the facial).

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the pharyngeal tonsil (adenoids). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: What is the cadaveric position of the vocal cords?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the cadaveric position of the vocal cords?
options: Cords adducted in the midline during phonation
Cords in the paramedian position on one side
Cords widely open during quiet breathing
body.explanation: If the recurrent and external laryngeal nerves are involved on both sides, all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed, the cords are further abducted and fixed. This is the cadaveric position of the vocal cords or rima glottidis.
option_notes: All nerves cut: cords half-open and still.
That is phonation.
That is one recurrent palsy.
That is normal breathing.

title: What are the two parts of the lacrimal gland?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What are the two parts of the lacrimal gland?
body.explanation: The gland is about 2 cm long. The orbital part is larger and sits on the lateral margin of the levator palpebrae superioris. The palpebral part is smaller and lies along the inner surface of the eyelid.

title: What do the intrinsic muscles of the tongue do?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What do the intrinsic muscles of the tongue do?
options: They move the tongue as a whole
body.explanation: Intrinsic muscles are confined to the tongue with no bony attachment: longitudinal, transverse and vertical fibres. Their function is to alter the shape of the tongue. Extrinsic muscles connect it to surrounding structures and help in its movements.

title: Through which opening does the facial nerve leave the skull?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Through which opening does the facial nerve leave the skull?
body.explanation: It exits via the stylomastoid foramen, enters the parotid gland and divides into its five purely motor branches.

title: Which arteries are terminal branches of the external carotid artery? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which arteries are terminal branches of the external carotid artery? (choose all)
body.explanation: The external carotid ends in the parotid gland by dividing into the maxillary and superficial temporal arteries. The facial and lingual arteries are branches given off earlier in the neck.

title: Where does the posterior white commissure run?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the posterior white commissure run?
options: Under the epiphysis, in the posterior wall of the third ventricle
In the floor of the fourth ventricle
body.explanation: The anterior commissure lies in front of the fornix; the posterior commissure passes under the pineal gland (epiphysis).
option_notes: Under the pineal gland, at the back of the third ventricle.
That is the anterior commissure.
It is a separate bundle.
Not there.

title: Which part of the retina is not sensitive to light?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which part of the retina is not sensitive to light?
body.explanation: The non-visual retina is the portion not sensitive to light: the anterior continuation of the pigment cell layer plus supporting cells over the ciliary body and the posterior surface of the iris.

title: Which sulcus lies between the highlighted gyri?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which sulcus lies between the highlighted gyri?
body.explanation: The central sulcus separates the precentral gyrus (motor) in front from the postcentral gyrus (sensory) behind.
option_notes: The central sulcus separates the precentral gyrus (motor) in front from the postcentral gyrus (sensory) behind.
The parieto-occipital sulcus separates the parietal and occipital lobes on the medial surface.
The cingulate sulcus runs above the cingulate gyrus on the medial surface.
The lateral sulcus (Sylvius) separates the temporal lobe from the frontal and parietal lobes.

title: Which functions does CSF perform?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which functions does CSF perform?
body.explanation: CSF provides nourishment, waste removal and protection to the brain.
option_notes: It cushions the brain.
It carries nutrients.
It clears waste.
CSF does not produce hormones.

title: How do the pretectal nuclei produce the consensual response?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How do the pretectal nuclei produce the consensual response?
options: They send fibres directly to both irises
They project to the visual cortex first
They act through the medial longitudinal fasciculus
They project to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei
body.explanation: The pretectal nuclei project to the ipsilateral Edinger-Westphal nucleus and also to the contralateral one via the posterior commissure. That is why light in one eye constricts both pupils.

title: Which surface groove of the spinal cord is deep?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which surface groove of the spinal cord is deep?
body.explanation: A deep anterior median fissure, a shallow posterior median sulcus, and anterolateral and posterolateral sulci where the root filaments emerge.
option_notes: Shallow.
The anterior fissure is deep.
Shallow.
Shallow.

title: Which valves modify the size of the nasal fossa? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which valves modify the size of the nasal fossa? (choose all)
body.explanation: Three valves regulate airflow: the nostril valve, the nasal valve and the septo-turbinal valve. They modify the size of the nasal fossa and so the resistance to airflow.

title: Which two bones form the roof of the orbit?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which two bones form the roof of the orbit?
options: Orbital plate of the frontal bone and lesser wing of the sphenoid
Orbital plate of the frontal bone and greater wing of the sphenoid
Orbital surface of the maxilla and lesser wing of the sphenoid
Orbital plate of the ethmoid and orbital plate of the frontal bone
body.explanation: The roof is the orbital plate of the frontal bone plus, posteriorly, the lesser wing of the sphenoid. The greater wing belongs to the lateral wall.

title: The glenoid (mandibular) fossa, which receives the head of the mandible, belongs to which bone?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The glenoid (mandibular) fossa, which receives the head of the mandible, belongs to which bone?
body.explanation: The mandibular (glenoid) fossa is on the squamous part of the temporal bone, just below the zygomatic process. Together with the head of the mandible it forms the temporomandibular joint.

title: Which type of strabismus is an inward turning of the eye?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which type of strabismus is an inward turning of the eye?
body.explanation: Esotropia: inward turning. Exotropia: outward turning. Hypotropia: downward turning. Hypertropia: upward turning.

title: Damage at the optic chiasm produces which visual defect?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Damage at the optic chiasm produces which visual defect?
options: Total loss of vision in one eye
Loss of the whole right side of vision
Loss of both outer visual fields
body.explanation: At the chiasm the crossing fibres are cut, so the temporal (lateral) portions of the visual field are lost in both eyes. The lecture describes this as damage at site 3.

title: Which nerve supplies the superior oblique muscle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerve supplies the superior oblique muscle?
body.explanation: The lecture lists: motor supply CN III, parasympathetic supply CN III, motor supply CN IV, motor supply CN VI. LR6 SO4 still applies.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the malleus. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: This is at the arrow: the outer ossicle, its handle attached to the eardrum.
Not at the arrow; this is air spaces in the mastoid behind the middle ear.
Not at the arrow; this is the snail-shaped hearing organ of the inner ear.
Not at the arrow; this is the inner ossicle, its footplate in the oval window.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the radial, axillary, ulnar, median. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Into which structure does the lacrimal fluid empty?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Into which structure does the lacrimal fluid empty?
body.explanation: The acini produce a watery serous secretion which is secreted into excretory ducts that empty into the superior conjunctival fornix. The fluid is then spread over the cornea by blinking.

title: Which muscle forms the lateral wall of the vestibule?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscle forms the lateral wall of the vestibule?
body.explanation: The lateral wall of the vestibule is formed by the cheek, which is composed of the buccinator muscle, covered laterally by the skin and medially by the mucous membrane.

title: Which sulcus lies between the highlighted gyri?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which sulcus lies between the highlighted gyri?
body.explanation: The lateral sulcus separates the superior temporal gyrus below from the frontal and parietal gyri above.
option_notes: The lateral sulcus separates the superior temporal gyrus below from the frontal and parietal gyri above.
The parieto-occipital sulcus separates the parietal and occipital lobes on the medial surface.
The intraparietal sulcus divides the superior from the inferior parietal lobule.
The calcarine sulcus runs on the medial occipital lobe between cuneus and lingual gyrus.

title: Which are the stated functions of the eyelashes (cilia)? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are the stated functions of the eyelashes (cilia)? (choose all)
options: Protecting the eyes from foreign particles
Preventing evaporation of the tear film
Producing the oil layer of the tear film
body.explanation: The lecture gives three functions for the cilia: protecting the eyes from foreign particles, preventing evaporation of the tear film, and acting as sensory receptors.

title: What forms the facial colliculus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the facial colliculus?
body.explanation: In the floor of the fourth ventricle, the facial colliculus is a bulge made by facial nerve fibres looping around the abducens nucleus.
option_notes: Makes the olive.
Midbrain.
Facial fibres loop around the abducens nucleus.
Not this.

title: The third ventricle lies:
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The third ventricle lies:
body.explanation: A median cleft in the diencephalon.
option_notes: Those hold the lateral ventricles.
That is the fourth ventricle region.
That holds the aqueduct.
A slit between the two thalami.

title: How long is the spinal cord?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How long is the spinal cord?
body.explanation: Length 40 to 45 cm, transverse diameter 10 to 12 mm, anteroposterior about 8 mm, mass 25 to 30 g.
option_notes: Too short.
Too long.
Too long.
About 40 to 45 cm.

title: Into which two major triangles is each side of the neck divided?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Into which two major triangles is each side of the neck divided?
body.explanation: Each side of the neck is divided into two major well-known triangles: the anterior triangle and the posterior triangle. Both are covered by the deep fascia of the neck, and only after its removal do the secondary triangles come into view.

title: What closes the nasopharyngeal isthmus during swallowing?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What closes the nasopharyngeal isthmus during swallowing?
body.explanation: In the second stage the nasopharyngeal isthmus is closed by elevation of the soft palate and contraction of Passavant's ridge, preventing food entering the nasopharynx. The laryngeal inlet is closed by approximation of the aryepiglottic folds.

title: Which are telencephalic commissures?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are telencephalic commissures?
body.explanation: The corpus callosum, fornix, anterior and posterior commissures. The internal capsule and centrum semiovale are projection white matter, not commissures.
option_notes: Joins the two hemispheres.
Joins the two hemispheres.
A projection pathway, not a commissure.
The white matter core of the hemisphere.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Mammillary bodies: the pair of round swellings behind the infundibulum (hypothalamus).
option_notes: Pineal gland is the small midline gland above the superior colliculi; secretes melatonin.
Optic chiasm is where the optic nerves meet and partly cross, in front of the hypothalamus.
Thalamus is the large paired grey mass of the diencephalon, the sensory relay.
The pair of round swellings behind the infundibulum (hypothalamus).

title: Which structure is the main bundle of fibres joining the two cerebral hemispheres?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is the main bundle of fibres joining the two cerebral hemispheres?
body.explanation: The corpus callosum is a white matter tract connecting the two hemispheres.
option_notes: The corpus callosum links the two hemispheres.
The internal capsule carries fibres up and down, not across.
The falx is a fold of dura, not nerve fibres.
The centrum semiovale is the white matter core of each hemisphere.

title: How many gyri make up the temporal lobe in this lecture's description?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How many gyri make up the temporal lobe in this lecture's description?
body.explanation: The temporal lobe has five gyri; the fifth, most medial, is the hippocampal gyrus.
option_notes: Five temporal gyri.
Three are visible on the lateral face only.
One short.
Six is the occipital count.

title: What forms the anterior two thirds of the floor of the nasal cavity?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the anterior two thirds of the floor of the nasal cavity?
options: The palatine process of the maxilla
The horizontal plate of the palatine bone
body.explanation: Floor: anterior two thirds, the palatine process of the maxillary bone; posterior third, the horizontal plate of the palatine bone.

title: Besides arachnoid granulations, what else contributes to CSF clearance?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Besides arachnoid granulations, what else contributes to CSF clearance?
options: Meningeal lymphatic vessels and perivascular pathways
body.explanation: CSF clearance is not only through arachnoid granulations; meningeal lymphatics and perivascular routes also contribute.
option_notes: These also drain CSF.
The choroid plexus makes CSF.
It is a channel, not a drain.
Not the route named.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the lateral (horizontal) semicircular canal. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the snail-shaped hearing organ of the inner ear.
This is at the arrow: the canal in the horizontal plane.
Not at the arrow; this is the duct from the vestibule ending in a sac under the dura.
Not at the arrow; this is the swelling at one end of each canal, holding the crista.

title: Which nerve supplies the muscles of mastication?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerve supplies the muscles of mastication?
body.explanation: All four muscles of mastication are supplied by branches of the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve.

title: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which gyrus or area is highlighted in orange?
options: Opercular part of the inferior frontal gyrus
body.explanation: Transverse temporal gyri (Heschl): the gyri on the upper surface of the temporal lobe, inside the lateral sulcus: the primary auditory cortex.
option_notes: Parahippocampal gyrus is the medial temporal gyrus on the inferior surface, ending in front in the uncus.
Opercular part of the inferior frontal gyrus is the back part of the inferior frontal gyrus; with the triangular part it forms Broca's area (dominant side).
Postcentral gyrus is the gyrus just behind the central sulcus: the primary somatosensory cortex.
The gyri on the upper surface of the temporal lobe, inside the lateral sulcus: the primary auditory cortex.

title: What proportion of the outer coat does the cornea form?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What proportion of the outer coat does the cornea form?
body.explanation: The cornea forms one sixth of the outer coat and the sclera the other five sixths.

title: Which part of the ventricular system is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which part of the ventricular system is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Third ventricle: the narrow midline ventricle between the two thalami.
option_notes: The narrow midline ventricle between the two thalami.
Cerebral aqueduct is the narrow channel through the midbrain from the third to the fourth ventricle.
Choroid plexus is the vascular tufts in the ventricles that produce CSF.
Fourth ventricle is the ventricle between the brainstem and cerebellum.

title: Which artery passes through the foramen spinosum to supply the dura mater?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which artery passes through the foramen spinosum to supply the dura mater?
body.explanation: The middle meningeal artery is a branch of the mandibular part of the maxillary artery. It enters the skull at the foramen spinosum and supplies the dura mater and calvaria.

title: Where do the muscles of facial expression insert?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where do the muscles of facial expression insert?
options: Into the periosteum of the facial bones
Into the skin and fascia of the face
Into the tendons of the muscles of mastication
Into the cartilage of the external ear
body.explanation: They lie in the superficial fascia, arise from bone or fascia and insert into the skin. That is why their contraction moves the skin and produces expressions.

title: Which cerebellar peduncle connects the pons to the cerebellum?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cerebellar peduncle connects the pons to the cerebellum?
body.explanation: Superior: midbrain. Middle: pons. Inferior: medulla oblongata.
option_notes: Joins the midbrain to the cerebellum.
Joins the medulla to the cerebellum.
Part of the midbrain, not cerebellar.
The middle peduncle joins the pons.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the superior concha. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which are the three major salivary glands? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are the three major salivary glands? (choose all)
body.explanation: The three major salivary glands are the parotid, submandibular and sublingual. The lacrimal gland makes tears, and the pterygopalatine is a ganglion, not a gland.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the optic nerve. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Hyoid bone: the U-shaped bone above the larynx.
option_notes: Epiglottis is the leaf-shaped cartilage behind the tongue base.
Trachea is the tube of C-shaped cartilage rings below the cricoid.
Arytenoid cartilages is the paired pyramids on the back of the cricoid where the vocal ligaments attach.
The U-shaped bone above the larynx.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Malleus: the outer ossicle, its handle attached to the eardrum.
option_notes: Cochlea is the snail-shaped hearing organ of the inner ear.
The outer ossicle, its handle attached to the eardrum.
Stapes is the smallest ossicle, its footplate in the oval window.
Facial nerve (VII) is the nerve running through the temporal bone in its own canal, close to the middle ear.

title: Which cranial nerve leaves the brainstem between the two cerebral peduncles?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cranial nerve leaves the brainstem between the two cerebral peduncles?
body.explanation: The oculomotor nerve exits from the interpeduncular fossa, between the peduncles.
option_notes: III emerges between the peduncles.
IV emerges from the back of the midbrain.
V emerges from the side of the pons.
XII emerges from the medulla.

title: Which functional area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which functional area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: The postcentral gyrus, behind the central sulcus, is the primary sensory cortex for touch, pain and temperature.
option_notes: Primary motor cortex lies in the precentral gyrus.
Primary auditory cortex lies in the transverse temporal gyri (Heschl).
Primary somatosensory cortex lies in the postcentral gyrus.
Broca's area (speech production) lies in the opercular and triangular parts of the inferior frontal gyrus.

title: Which structure is NOT part of the diencephalon?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is NOT part of the diencephalon?
body.explanation: Your professor's question. The diencephalon has four parts: epithalamus, thalamus, subthalamus and hypothalamus. The pons belongs to the brainstem.
option_notes: The pons belongs to the brainstem.
The thalamus is diencephalon.
The hypothalamus is diencephalon.
The epithalamus is diencephalon.

title: Which functional area is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which functional area is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: The banks of the calcarine sulcus, between cuneus and lingual gyrus, hold the primary visual cortex.
option_notes: Primary auditory cortex lies in the transverse temporal gyri (Heschl).
Primary motor cortex lies in the precentral gyrus.
Primary visual cortex lies in the banks of the calcarine sulcus.
Broca's area (speech production) lies in the opercular and triangular parts of the inferior frontal gyrus.

title: On which face of the hemisphere is the calcarine fissure?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: On which face of the hemisphere is the calcarine fissure?
body.explanation: The calcarine fissure is a long horizontal groove on the internal face, from the occipital pole to the internal parieto-occipital sulcus.
option_notes: The calcarine fissure is on the medial face.
Not on the lateral face.
Not only inferior.
Not frontal.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Anterior (ventral) horn: grey matter with the motor neurons.
option_notes: Grey matter with the motor neurons.
Posterior (dorsal) horn is grey matter receiving sensory fibres.
Gracile fasciculus is the medial part of the dorsal column: fine touch and position sense from the lower body.
Posterior spinocerebellar tract is unconscious proprioception to the cerebellum, at the edge of the lateral funiculus.

title: What is the average weight of the cerebrum?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the average weight of the cerebrum?
body.explanation: Ovoid; width 14 cm, length 16 cm, height 12 cm; weight 1200 to 1400 g; greyish white; soft and crumbly.
option_notes: Too light.
Too heavy.
Too light.
About 1200 to 1400 g.

title: Which lobe is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which lobe is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Temporal lobe: below the lateral sulcus.
option_notes: The parietal lobe lies behind the central sulcus, above the lateral sulcus, in front of the parieto-occipital sulcus.
The occipital lobe lies at the back, behind the parieto-occipital sulcus.
The frontal lobe lies in front of the central sulcus and above the lateral sulcus.
The temporal lobe lies below the lateral sulcus.

title: Which tract carries fine touch and proprioception (position sense)?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which tract carries fine touch and proprioception (position sense)?
body.explanation: The dorsal columns carry fine touch and proprioception; the spinothalamic tracts carry pain and temperature.
option_notes: Dorsal columns: touch and position.
Spinothalamic: pain and temperature.
Corticospinal: voluntary movement.
Vestibulospinal: balance and posture.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the optic nerve. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which bones form the hard palate?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which bones form the hard palate?
body.explanation: The hard palate lies in the roof of the oral cavity and forms the floor of the nasal cavity. It is formed by the palatine processes of the maxillae in front and the horizontal plates of the palatine bones behind, and is bounded by the alveolar arches.

title: The levator palpebrae superioris is supplied by which nerve?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The levator palpebrae superioris is supplied by which nerve?
options: Abducens nerve (CN VI), the lateral rectus nerve
body.explanation: It arises from the lesser wing of the sphenoid above the optic canal and inserts into the superior tarsal plate. Unlike the facial muscles around it, it is supplied by CN III.

title: What does dopamine deficiency cause?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does dopamine deficiency cause?
body.explanation: Parkinson's disease: dopamine falls, acetylcholine becomes relatively high, giving rigidity, tremor and slowness. Anticholinergic drugs help restore balance.

title: Where is the grey matter of the hemisphere found?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where is the grey matter of the hemisphere found?
options: In the cortex and basal ganglia
Only in the internal capsule region
body.explanation: Grey matter lies in the peripheral cortex and the deep basal ganglia. White matter forms the centrum semiovale and the capsules.
option_notes: That is white matter.
In the cortex and the deep basal ganglia.
That is white matter.
Not only there.

title: What are the contents of Beclard's triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What are the contents of Beclard's triangle?
options: The carotid bifurcation and a lymph node
The submandibular gland and facial vein
body.explanation: Beclard's triangle is also known as the posterior triangle of the lingual artery. Its contents are the lingual artery and the hypoglossal nerve. Sometimes the arcus raninus, the anastomosis between the right and left end branches of the deep lingual artery, is also present. The triangle helps in ligating the external carotid artery.

title: Into how many parts is the maxillary artery conventionally divided?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Into how many parts is the maxillary artery conventionally divided?
body.explanation: The maxillary artery is divided into three parts by the lateral pterygoid muscle: mandibular, pterygoid and pterygopalatine. Five branches come from each part.

title: Absence of the corneal reflex may indicate what?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Absence of the corneal reflex may indicate what?
options: Deep coma or a nerve lesion
body.explanation: Absence of the corneal reflex may indicate deep coma or stroke, either unilaterally or bilaterally. Unilateral loss may also indicate a lesion involving the trigeminal or facial nerve. Repeat the test on the other eye and document it.

title: Which structure controls autonomic and endocrine activity?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure controls autonomic and endocrine activity?
body.explanation: Your professor's question. The hypothalamus interfaces with the pituitary to control endocrine activity and holds autonomic control centres.
option_notes: It controls the autonomic system and the pituitary.
Sensory relay.
Movement.
Movement.

title: What is the modiolus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the modiolus?
options: A membrane closing the oval window
A duct joining utricle and saccule
The apex opening of the cochlea
body.explanation: The modiolus is the axial bony stem around which the cochlear canal spirals. Its base lies at the fundus of the internal acoustic meatus and is perforated by fibres of the cochlear nerve.
option_notes: The stapes closes the oval window.
That is the utriculo-saccular duct.
That is the helicotrema.
The bony pillar the cochlea spirals around.

title: What does a lesion of the right optic tract cause?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does a lesion of the right optic tract cause?
body.explanation: Each optic tract carries the contralateral visual field of both eyes, so an optic tract lesion gives a contralateral homonymous hemianopia.

title: Which extrapyramidal tracts cross the midline?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which extrapyramidal tracts cross the midline?
body.explanation: The rubrospinal and tectospinal tracts decussate, giving contralateral innervation; the others are ipsilateral.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the anterior (ventral) horn: motor. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the tiny canal in the middle of the grey matter.
Not at the arrow; this is the outer white columns of fibre tracts.
Not at the arrow; this is the narrow back horn receiving sensory fibres.
This is at the arrow: the broad front horn of motor neurons.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Cricoid cartilage: the only complete cartilage ring, below the thyroid cartilage.
option_notes: Arytenoid cartilages is the paired pyramids on the back of the cricoid where the vocal ligaments attach.
The only complete cartilage ring, below the thyroid cartilage.
Thyroid gland is the butterfly-shaped gland on the front of the trachea, two lobes joined by an isthmus.
Thyroid cartilage is the large shield-shaped cartilage with the laryngeal prominence.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the retina. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: What is the suspensory ligament of Berry?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the suspensory ligament of Berry?
options: A ligament between the hyoid and the thyroid cartilage
The band joining the isthmus to the sternum
A thickening of the false capsule
A fold of pretracheal fascia over the trachea
body.explanation: On the medial surface of the thyroid lobe the false capsule thickens to form the suspensory ligament of Berry, connecting the lobe to the cricoid cartilage.
option_notes: That is the thyrohyoid membrane.
Not this.
A thickening of the false capsule fixing the gland to the cricoid.
It is a thickening, not a fold over the trachea.

title: Into which sinuses do the cerebellar veins drain?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Into which sinuses do the cerebellar veins drain?
options: Superior petrosal, transverse and straight sinuses
body.explanation: The superior and inferior cerebellar veins drain into the superior petrosal, transverse and straight sinuses.
option_notes: These three sinuses.
Not the cavernous sinus.
Not the superior sagittal sinus.
They drain via the sinuses first.

title: What divides the thalamus into three main parts?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What divides the thalamus into three main parts?
body.explanation: A Y-shaped sheet of white matter, the internal medullary lamina, divides each thalamus into anterior, medial and lateral parts.
option_notes: The external capsule is lateral to the putamen.
It joins the two thalami.
Not this.
The Y-shaped internal medullary lamina divides it.

title: Which arteries supply the nasal septum? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which arteries supply the nasal septum? (choose all)
body.explanation: The septum is supplied by septal branches of the anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteries, the sphenopalatine, the greater palatine and the superior labial arteries. That mix of internal and external carotid branches explains the frequency of epistaxis.

title: Through which structure do the pyramidal (corticospinal) fibres pass after leaving the motor cortex, so that a small stroke there can paralyse a whole side?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Through which structure do the pyramidal (corticospinal) fibres pass after leaving the motor cortex, so that a small stroke there can paralyse a whole side?
body.explanation: The corticospinal tracts converge in the internal capsule, then run through the cerebral peduncles to the brainstem.
option_notes: The fibres are packed tightly here, so a small lesion has a big effect.
The corpus callosum joins the hemispheres.
The external capsule lies outside the lentiform nucleus.
The fornix is a limbic pathway.

title: Which is NOT part of the membranous labyrinth?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which is NOT part of the membranous labyrinth?
body.explanation: The membranous labyrinth comprises the semicircular ducts, the cochlear duct, the utricle and the saccule. The modiolus is the bony central pillar of the cochlea.
option_notes: The utricle is membranous.
The saccule is membranous.
The cochlear duct is membranous.
The modiolus is the bony core of the cochlea.

title: What bounds the subthalamus laterally?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What bounds the subthalamus laterally?
body.explanation: The subthalamus lies below the thalamus and above the midbrain: medially the hypothalamus, laterally the internal capsule, posteriorly the red nucleus and substantia nigra.
option_notes: The internal capsule lies lateral.
Medial.
Not the lateral boundary.
Medial.

title: What is the correct order of CSF flow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the correct order of CSF flow?
options: Lateral ventricles, foramina of Monro, third ventricle, aqueduct, fourth ventricle, subarachnoid space
Third ventricle, lateral ventricles, fourth ventricle, aqueduct, subarachnoid space
Fourth ventricle, aqueduct, third ventricle, lateral ventricles
Subarachnoid space, lateral ventricles, third ventricle, fourth ventricle
body.explanation: CSF flows from the lateral ventricles through Monro to the third, through the aqueduct to the fourth, then out to the subarachnoid space.
option_notes: This is the one-way flow.
The lateral ventricles come first.
This is backwards.
CSF reaches the subarachnoid space last.

title: Which muscle contracts in the corneal reflex, and which nerve drives it?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscle contracts in the corneal reflex, and which nerve drives it?
options: Levator palpebrae superioris, through CN III
Superior tarsal muscle, through sympathetic fibres
Ciliary muscle, through the ciliary ganglion
body.explanation: The facial motor nucleus is activated on both sides, so touching one cornea makes both eyes blink through the orbicularis oculi.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the posterior triangle. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which part of the eardrum lacks the fibrous layer?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which part of the eardrum lacks the fibrous layer?
body.explanation: In the pars flaccida (Shrapnell's membrane) the middle fibrous layer is replaced by loose areolar tissue, so it is thin, lax and slightly pinkish.
option_notes: The pars tensa has a fibrous layer.
The annulus is a fibrous ring.
The pars flaccida lacks the middle fibrous layer.
The umbo is on the pars tensa.

title: How many nerve fibres does the corpus callosum contain?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How many nerve fibres does the corpus callosum contain?
body.explanation: The corpus callosum is a white matter tract of about 200 million fibres connecting the lobes of the two hemispheres.
option_notes: Too few.
Too many.
Too few.
About 200 million fibres.

title: Which is the largest paranasal sinus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which is the largest paranasal sinus?
body.explanation: There is one on each side, and it is the largest of the paranasal sinuses, about 3.5 x 2.5 x 3.5 cm. It completely fills the body of the maxilla and is pyramidal in shape.

title: Which are ascending conscious tracts?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are ascending conscious tracts?
body.explanation: Conscious: dorsal column-medial lemniscus and anterolateral system. Unconscious: spinocerebellar tracts. The corticospinal tract is descending.
option_notes: Conscious touch and position.
Conscious pain and temperature.
Unconscious proprioception.
Descending motor.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the soft palate. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: What is strabismus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is strabismus?
body.explanation: A squint occurs when the eyes don't point in the same direction. The most common type is where one eye turns slightly inwards, towards the nose. Squints affect about one in 20 children.

title: Which cranial nerve is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cranial nerve is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Vagus nerve (X): leaves the medulla behind the olive, below IX.
option_notes: Facial nerve (VII) is leaves at the cerebellopontine angle, with VIII.
Abducens nerve (VI) is leaves at the pontomedullary junction, near the midline.
Hypoglossal nerve (XII) is leaves the medulla between the pyramid and the olive.
Leaves the medulla behind the olive, below IX.

title: Which are the three anatomical lobes of the cerebellum?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are the three anatomical lobes of the cerebellum?
body.explanation: Two fissures (primary and posterolateral) divide the cerebellum into anterior, posterior and flocculonodular lobes.
option_notes: The three cerebellar lobes.
These are cerebral lobes.
These are the peduncles.
These are longitudinal zones, not lobes.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the cricoid cartilage. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is an inconstant extension rising from the isthmus.
This is at the arrow: the complete ring below the thyroid cartilage.
Not at the arrow; this is the lateral lobe on the patient's left (viewer's right).
Not at the arrow; this is the external carotid branch reaching the upper pole.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Thalamus: the large paired grey mass on either side of the third ventricle.
option_notes: The large paired grey mass on either side of the third ventricle.
Hypothalamus is the region below the thalamus, forming the floor of the third ventricle.
Caudate nucleus is the C-shaped nucleus curving along the lateral ventricle.
Cerebral aqueduct is the narrow channel through the midbrain from the third to the fourth ventricle.

title: What lines the paranasal sinuses?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What lines the paranasal sinuses?
body.explanation: The sinuses are lined by a respiratory epithelium, continuous with the lining of the nasal cavity.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the tympanic membrane (eardrum). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the snail-shaped hearing organ of the inner ear.
Not at the arrow; this is the three looped canals for balance.
This is at the arrow: the thin membrane closing the inner end of the canal.
