Not at the arrow; this is the air space behind the eardrum holding the ossicles.

title: Which extraocular muscle does NOT arise from the orbital apex?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which extraocular muscle does NOT arise from the orbital apex?
body.explanation: The inferior oblique arises from the orbital surface of the maxilla, near the front of the floor. All the others arise at the apex (common tendinous ring, body of sphenoid or lesser wing).

title: Which tract carries voluntary motor commands down the spinal cord?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which tract carries voluntary motor commands down the spinal cord?
body.explanation: Descending tracts carry motor information; the corticospinal tract controls voluntary movement.
option_notes: Corticospinal: voluntary movement.
Spinothalamic is sensory.
Dorsal columns are sensory.
Spinocerebellar tracts are sensory to the cerebellum.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the posterior (dorsal) horn: sensory. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the deep groove on the front of the cord.
Not at the arrow; this is the broad front horn of motor neurons.
This is at the arrow: the narrow back horn receiving sensory fibres.
Not at the arrow; this is the outer white columns of fibre tracts.

title: What forms the lateral boundary of the anterior triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the lateral boundary of the anterior triangle?
body.explanation: The anterior triangle is bounded laterally by the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid, medially by the midline, and superiorly by the lower border of the mandible.

title: Which of these is a cranial bone rather than a facial bone?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which of these is a cranial bone rather than a facial bone?
body.explanation: The 8 cranial bones are the frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, 2 parietals and 2 temporals. The others listed are facial bones.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the third ventricle. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the top of the brainstem, below the diencephalon.
Not at the arrow; this is the region below the thalamus forming the floor of the third ventricle.
This is at the arrow: the narrow midline cavity between the two thalami.
Not at the arrow; this is the gland hanging from the infundibulum in the sella.

title: Which layer of the meninges is the deepest, lying directly on the spinal cord?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which layer of the meninges is the deepest, lying directly on the spinal cord?
body.explanation: From outside in: dura, arachnoid, pia. The pia is the deepest.
option_notes: The pia covers the cord directly.
The dura is the outermost.
The arachnoid is the middle layer.
The periosteum lines the bone.

title: Where does the right common carotid artery arise?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the right common carotid artery arise?
options: Directly from the arch of the aorta
body.explanation: The right common carotid arises from the brachiocephalic trunk behind the sternoclavicular joint. The left arises directly from the arch of the aorta.

title: Endoscopic third ventriculostomy creates an opening:
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Endoscopic third ventriculostomy creates an opening:
options: In the floor of the third ventricle to the interpeduncular cistern
Between the fourth ventricle and the cisterna magna
From the lateral ventricle to the peritoneum
body.explanation: The lateral ventricle to peritoneum route is a shunt, not ETV.
option_notes: A hole in the floor to the interpeduncular cistern bypasses the aqueduct.
Not this.
Not this.
That is a shunt.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the optic chiasm. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which are functions of the Eustachian tube?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are functions of the Eustachian tube?
body.explanation: The lecture gives three functions: maintaining equilibrium of air pressure, protection, and drainage.
option_notes: It equalises pressure on both sides of the drum.
It drains middle ear secretions.
The ossicles amplify sound.
Balance is the inner ear.

title: Which type of secretory unit predominates in the submandibular gland?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which type of secretory unit predominates in the submandibular gland?
body.explanation: The submandibular (submaxillary) gland is the second largest and is a mixed gland with both serous and mucous units, but serous units predominate. The sublingual gland is also mixed, but mucous units predominate there.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the middle concha. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Into how many air channels do the conchae divide each nasal cavity?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Into how many air channels do the conchae divide each nasal cavity?
body.explanation: The conchae divide each nasal cavity into four air channels: the inferior, middle and superior meatuses and the spheno-ethmoidal recess.

title: Where does the ethmoidal sinus drain its lymph?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the ethmoidal sinus drain its lymph?
body.explanation: Primary lymphatic drainage: submandibular lymph nodes for the anterior and middle ethmoid sinuses, and retropharyngeal lymph nodes for the posterior ethmoid sinus.

title: Which belong to the posterior (balance) labyrinth?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which belong to the posterior (balance) labyrinth?
body.explanation: The posterior labyrinth, for balance, includes the utricle, saccule, semicircular ducts and endolymphatic system. The anterior labyrinth, for hearing, is the cochlear duct.
option_notes: The utricle is a balance organ.
The semicircular ducts serve balance.
The cochlear duct is the hearing (anterior) labyrinth.
The spiral lamina is in the cochlea.

title: Which nuclei belong to the basal ganglia?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nuclei belong to the basal ganglia?
body.explanation: Five pairs: caudate, putamen, globus pallidus, subthalamic nucleus and substantia nigra.
option_notes: The caudate is a basal ganglion.
The putamen is a basal ganglion.
The thalamus is diencephalon.
The hippocampus is limbic cortex.

title: Where is the dopamine of the extrapyramidal system made?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where is the dopamine of the extrapyramidal system made?
body.explanation: Dopamine is produced by the substantia nigra pars compacta and acts mainly on the striatum, smoothing voluntary movement.

title: The two bellies of the occipitofrontalis are joined by which structure?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The two bellies of the occipitofrontalis are joined by which structure?
body.explanation: The frontal and occipital bellies are connected by the intervening tendinous sheet, the galea aponeurotica (epicranial aponeurosis). The frontal belly has no bony attachment.

title: What forms the inferior boundary of Beclard's triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the inferior boundary of Beclard's triangle?
options: The greater cornu of the hyoid bone
body.explanation: Beclard's triangle is bounded inferiorly by the greater cornu of the hyoid bone, superiorly by the posterior belly of digastric, and posteriorly by the posterior border of hyoglossus, which forms its base.

title: Which muscle of the soft palate is supplied by the mandibular nerve?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscle of the soft palate is supplied by the mandibular nerve?
body.explanation: Tensor veli palatini: origin the spine of the sphenoid and auditory tube, supplied by the medial pterygoid nerve of the mandibular nerve, tensing the soft palate. All the other palatine muscles take the pharyngeal plexus.

title: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is highlighted in orange?
body.explanation: Corpus callosum: the large arched band of white matter joining the two hemispheres.
option_notes: Postcentral gyrus is the gyrus just behind the central sulcus: the primary somatosensory cortex.
Paracentral lobule is the medial continuation of the precentral and postcentral gyri (leg area).
Temporal pole is the front tip of the temporal lobe.
The large arched band of white matter joining the two hemispheres.

title: Which artery gives the anterior and posterior spinal arteries?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which artery gives the anterior and posterior spinal arteries?
body.explanation: The vertebral artery gives the anterior and posterior spinal arteries; segmental arteries give 31 pairs of radicular branches.
option_notes: Both spinal arteries come from the vertebral artery.
Not the source.
The aorta gives radicular arteries.
Anterior circulation.

title: Which bones meet at the pterion? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which bones meet at the pterion? (choose all)
body.explanation: The pterion is the H-shaped junction of the frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and greater wing of the sphenoid. The occipital and ethmoid take no part in it.

title: What is the hypothalamus's most basic function?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the hypothalamus's most basic function?
body.explanation: It maintains a steady internal state: hunger, thirst, temperature, blood pressure and heart rate. It links the nervous and endocrine systems and controls the stress response.
option_notes: The thalamus relays vision.
Not its role.
It keeps the internal environment stable.
The pineal does this.

title: The superior oblique tendon passes through which structure?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The superior oblique tendon passes through which structure?
body.explanation: The superior oblique arises from the body of the sphenoid. Its tendon passes through a fibrous ring, the trochlea, which changes its direction before it inserts deep to the superior rectus muscle.

title: A patient speaks fluently but makes no sense and does not understand what is said to them. Which area is damaged?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: A patient speaks fluently but makes no sense and does not understand what is said to them. Which area is damaged?
body.explanation: Wernicke's area, in the posterior superior temporal lobe, is for understanding language.
option_notes: Wernicke's area is for understanding language.
Broca's damage gives non-fluent speech with good understanding.
That is the motor strip.
The insula is not the language comprehension area.

title: Which muscle does the lens use to change shape in accommodation?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which muscle does the lens use to change shape in accommodation?
body.explanation: In the near response the ciliary muscles contract, the suspensory ligament relaxes, the lens becomes more convex and the dioptric power of the eye increases, so the near object focuses on the retina.

title: Which are the four parts of the diencephalon?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are the four parts of the diencephalon?
options: Caudate, putamen, globus pallidus and claustrum
Cortex, white matter, ventricles and meninges
body.explanation: The diencephalon is divided into the epithalamus, thalamus, subthalamus and hypothalamus.
option_notes: These four make up the diencephalon.
These are the brainstem and cerebellum.
These are basal ganglia and nearby grey matter.
These are general brain layers, not diencephalic parts.

title: How many neurons make up the pyramidal pathway?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How many neurons make up the pyramidal pathway?
body.explanation: A fast pathway of two neurons: N1, the upper motor neuron (pyramidal cells), and N2, the lower motor neuron in the ventral horn or a brainstem motor nucleus.

title: CSF is found in the:
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: CSF is found in the:
options: Space between the two layers of dura
body.explanation: The dural venous sinuses lie between the dural layers.
option_notes: CSF circulates in the subarachnoid space.
Potential space.
Fat, not CSF.
Holds the venous sinuses.

title: Which of these are parts of the diencephalon?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which of these are parts of the diencephalon?
body.explanation: The diencephalon has four parts: epithalamus, thalamus, subthalamus and hypothalamus (slide 4).
option_notes: Correct: pineal gland, habenular nuclei, stria medullaris.
Correct: lies below the thalamus, lateral to the hypothalamus.
Part of the brainstem (metencephalon).
Part of the hindbrain, behind the brainstem.

title: Which joint is functionally the most important?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which joint is functionally the most important?
body.explanation: The cricoarytenoid joint is an elliptical synovial articulation reinforced by the posterior cricoarytenoid ligament. Its rotatory movement abducts or adducts the vocal cords, and its gliding movement opens or closes the posterior part of the glottis.
option_notes: It tilts the cricoid but matters less.
Not a true joint.
It moves the arytenoids and so the cords.
Not a key joint.

title: Which artery is the main supply of the tongue?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which artery is the main supply of the tongue?
body.explanation: Arteries: the lingual artery, the tonsillar branch of the facial artery and the ascending pharyngeal artery. Veins: the lingual vein, which ultimately drains into the internal jugular vein.

title: What divides the submandibular triangle into anterior and posterior parts?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What divides the submandibular triangle into anterior and posterior parts?
body.explanation: The submandibular triangle is bordered superiorly by the inferior border of the body of the mandible and lies between the anterior and posterior bellies of digastric. It is subdivided into anterior and posterior parts by the stylomandibular ligament.

title: Which meningeal space contains CSF?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which meningeal space contains CSF?
body.explanation: The meninges are dura, arachnoid and pia from outside in. The subarachnoid space, between arachnoid and pia, holds CSF.
option_notes: Fat and veins.
A potential space.
Not a meningeal space.
CSF is in the subarachnoid space.

title: Which tonsils are found in the oropharynx?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which tonsils are found in the oropharynx?
body.explanation: The oropharynx contains the palatine tonsils, between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches, and the lingual tonsil on the back of the tongue.

title: Where does the temporal horn of the lateral ventricle end?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the temporal horn of the lateral ventricle end?
body.explanation: The temporal horn runs forward from the atrium below the thalamus and ends at the amygdala.
option_notes: It ends at the amygdala.
That is the occipital horn's direction.
Monro is at the front of the body.
The septum is medial to the frontal horn.

title: Where does the pyramidal (corticospinal) tract cross to the other side?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where does the pyramidal (corticospinal) tract cross to the other side?
options: In the spinal cord's anterior horn
body.explanation: The corticospinal tract descends from the motor cortex through the internal capsule to the medullary pyramid, where it crosses: the left cortex controls the right body.
option_notes: It crosses at the pyramids.
It passes through without crossing.
It starts there.
It ends near there.

title: What forms the posterior boundary of Farabeuf's triangle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What forms the posterior boundary of Farabeuf's triangle?
body.explanation: Farabeuf's triangle is bounded posteriorly by the internal jugular vein, anteroinferiorly by the common facial vein, and superiorly by the hypoglossal nerve, which forms its base.

title: What happens to the lens during parasympathetic stimulation (CN III)?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What happens to the lens during parasympathetic stimulation (CN III)?
options: The ciliary muscles relax, the zonules tighten and the lens flattens for distance
The lens moves backward toward the retina
The pupil widens and the lens is unaffected
The ciliary muscles contract, the zonules relax and the lens thickens
body.explanation: CN III parasympathetic stimulation produces sphincter-like contraction of the ciliary muscles, the ring becomes smaller, the zonules relax, and the lens relaxes and thickens: accommodation for near vision.

title: What shape is each lateral lobe?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What shape is each lateral lobe?
body.explanation: Each lateral lobe is a triangular pyramid with a tapered apex (upper pole) resting against the posterior and inferior part of the thyroid cartilage, a rounded base (lower pole) one or two centimetres from the sternum, and three sides.
option_notes: Each lobe is a triangular pyramid.
Not a disc.
Not hollow.
That is the cricoid.

title: In which cranial fossa does the brainstem lie?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: In which cranial fossa does the brainstem lie?
body.explanation: It lies in the posterior cranial fossa on the clivus, under the tentorium cerebelli, below the cerebrum and in front of the cerebellum.
option_notes: Holds the frontal lobes.
The brainstem lies in the posterior fossa.
Holds the temporal lobes.
Holds the pituitary.

title: Which part of the thalamus relays vision from the retina to the occipital cortex?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which part of the thalamus relays vision from the retina to the occipital cortex?
body.explanation: The lateral geniculate body receives the optic tract and projects to the visual cortex through the optic radiations.
option_notes: LGB: light (vision).
The MGB relays hearing.
The mammillary bodies are hypothalamic.
The habenula is epithalamic.

title: Which is the largest major salivary gland?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which is the largest major salivary gland?
body.explanation: The parotid (para = around, otic = ear) is the largest major salivary gland. It is purely serous and weighs about 15 grams. Its superficial portion lies in front of the external ear, and its deeper part fills the retromolar fossa.

title: Which nerve gives sensation to the floor of the mouth?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerve gives sensation to the floor of the mouth?
options: The buccal nerve, a branch of V3
The greater palatine nerve, from V2
body.explanation: Sensory supply of the oral cavity: roof, the greater palatine and nasopalatine nerves (branches of the maxillary nerve); floor, the lingual nerve (branch of the mandibular nerve); cheek, the buccal nerve (branch of the mandibular nerve).

title: What is the aqueous fluid?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the aqueous fluid?
options: A jelly-like substance filling the posterior segment
A lipid secretion of the meibomian glands
A layer of the tear film
body.explanation: Aqueous fluid is a clear plasma-derived ultrafiltrate, normally devoid of proteins, cells or other macromolecules.

title: Which cells make myelin in the central nervous system?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cells make myelin in the central nervous system?
body.explanation: Oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS axons; Schwann cells myelinate PNS axons.
option_notes: CNS myelin.
Schwann cells make PNS myelin.
Microglia are immune cells.
Ependymal cells line the ventricles.

title: What does the hypothalamus regulate?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the hypothalamus regulate?
body.explanation: It controls hunger, thirst, body temperature, blood pressure, heart rate, sexual activity and the stress response.
option_notes: It sets body temperature.
It controls hunger and thirst.
Thalamus.
Thalamus.

title: The infraorbital nerve is a continuation of which nerve?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: The infraorbital nerve is a continuation of which nerve?
body.explanation: The maxillary nerve enters the orbit via the inferior orbital fissure and continues as the infraorbital nerve, which leaves through the infraorbital foramen onto the face.

title: Which nerves supply the ethmoidal sinus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerves supply the ethmoidal sinus?
options: The supraorbital and supratrochlear nerves only
The infraorbital and alveolar nerves only
body.explanation: It is innervated by the anterior and posterior ethmoidal branches of the nasociliary nerve from the ophthalmic nerve (V1), and by the maxillary nerve (V2) via orbital branches from the pterygopalatine ganglion.

title: Which nerves make up the pharyngeal plexus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerves make up the pharyngeal plexus?
options: CN V, CN VII and CN XII together
CN X and CN XI only
CN IX, CN X and sympathetics
CN VII, CN IX and CN XI
body.explanation: The pharyngeal plexus is composed of the glossopharyngeal nerve, the vagus nerve and sympathetic fibres from the superior cervical ganglion.

title: What are the parathyroid glands like?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What are the parathyroid glands like?
options: A single midline gland behind the isthmus
Large glands the size of the thyroid lobes
Lymph nodes in the thyroid space
body.explanation: They are small endocrine glands, orange-yellow in colour and flattened, located in the fat of the thyroid space.
option_notes: They are usually four.
They are tiny.
They are not lymph nodes.
Small, flat, yellowish-brown glands.

title: How is the pinna pulled to examine the canal and drum?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How is the pinna pulled to examine the canal and drum?
body.explanation: Pulling the pinna upwards, backwards and laterally straightens the S-shaped canal so the tympanic membrane can be seen.
option_notes: This would narrow the canal in adults.
Backwards alone is not enough.
Forwards does not straighten the canal.
Up, back and out straightens the S-shaped canal in adults.

title: Besides the mandible, which facial bone is unpaired?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Besides the mandible, which facial bone is unpaired?
body.explanation: The facial skeleton has 6 paired bones (maxilla, zygomatic, palatine, nasal, lacrimal, inferior nasal concha) and 2 unpaired bones: the mandible and the vomer.

title: Which structures are found on the inner surface of the body of the mandible? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structures are found on the inner surface of the body of the mandible? (choose all)
body.explanation: The sublingual and submandibular fossae lie on the inner surface, above and below the mylohyoid line. The mental foramen is on the outer surface and the coronoid process is on the ramus.

title: What is the largest mastoid cell called?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the largest mastoid cell called?
body.explanation: The mastoid cells are air cells in the mastoid bone. The antrum is the most developed, and all cells communicate with each other and with the tympanic cavity.
option_notes: The antrum is the largest mastoid cell.
The aditus is the passage to it.
The tegmen is the roof.
The promontory is on the medial wall.

title: What is nystagmus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is nystagmus?
options: An inability to close the eye
A loss of the corneal reflex
body.explanation: Nystagmus is a vision condition in which the eyes make repetitive, uncontrolled movements, often resulting in reduced vision and depth perception, and it can affect balance and coordination. It is typically caused by brain injuries and results from brain damage.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the right lobe (lateral lobe). The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the complete ring below the thyroid cartilage.
Not at the arrow; this is the band joining the two lobes over tracheal rings 2 to 4.
Not at the arrow; this is the lateral lobe on the patient's left (viewer's right).
This is at the arrow: the lateral lobe on the patient's right (viewer's left).

title: Which structures lie superior to the cerebellum?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structures lie superior to the cerebellum?
options: The straight sinus and the great cerebral vein of Galen
body.explanation: Above the cerebellum: the great cerebral vein, the straight sinus in the tentorium, and the occipital lobe.
option_notes: Superior relations.
The occipital lobe lies above the tentorium.
The foramen magnum is below.
The fourth ventricle is in front.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the optic nerve. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which inputs feed the corticospinal tract? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which inputs feed the corticospinal tract? (choose all)
body.explanation: Primary motor cortex, premotor cortex and supplementary motor area.

title: Which cranial nerve emerges from the dorsal brainstem?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cranial nerve emerges from the dorsal brainstem?
body.explanation: Your professor's own question. CN IV is the only nerve emerging from the posterior surface, below the colliculi.
option_notes: IV is the only nerve leaving the back.
Ventral pons.
Ventral.
Ventral.

title: What does the tentorium cerebelli separate?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What does the tentorium cerebelli separate?
body.explanation: The tentorium divides the cranial cavity into a supratentorial compartment for the cerebrum and an infratentorial one for the cerebellum and brainstem.
option_notes: That is the falx cerebri.
Not a dural fold function.
It is a dural tent between cerebrum and cerebellum.
Lobes are separated by sulci.

title: What do the vortex veins drain?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What do the vortex veins drain?
body.explanation: The vortex veins carry the venous drainage of the uveal tract and pierce the sclera posterior to the globe's equator, draining into the two main veins.

title: Which geniculate body relays vision?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which geniculate body relays vision?
body.explanation: The LGB receives visual input from the retina via the optic tract and relays it via the optic radiations to the occipital cortex. The MGB relays hearing from the inferior colliculus to the temporal cortex.
option_notes: The medial body relays hearing.
Not the relay.
Limbic, not visual.
The lateral geniculate body relays vision.

title: How many bone pieces make up the lateral wall?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: How many bone pieces make up the lateral wall?
body.explanation: Six: the medial side of the maxillary body, the medial side of the frontal process of the maxilla, the medial aspect of the ethmoid, the lacrimal bone, the perpendicular plate of the palatine bone and the medial plate of the pterygoid process.

title: Where do the anterior columns of the fornix end?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Where do the anterior columns of the fornix end?
body.explanation: The fornix is a C-shaped white matter bundle under the corpus callosum, the main pathway of the hippocampus. Its anterior columns join the mammillary bodies; its posterior columns end at the hippocampus.
option_notes: They end in the mammillary bodies.
The fornix starts at the hippocampus.
Not their end.
Not their end.

title: Which are parts of the malleus?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are parts of the malleus?
body.explanation: Malleus: head, neck, manubrium, lateral and anterior processes. The lenticular process belongs to the incus, the footplate to the stapes.
option_notes: The handle (manubrium) is part of the malleus.
The lateral process is part of the malleus.
The lenticular process belongs to the incus.
The footplate belongs to the stapes.

title: Which bones take part in the floor of the orbit? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which bones take part in the floor of the orbit? (choose all)
body.explanation: The floor is formed by the orbital surface of the maxilla, the zygomatic bone and the orbital process of the palatine. The lacrimal and ethmoid belong to the medial wall.

title: Which cells continue as the optic nerve of the eye?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which cells continue as the optic nerve of the eye?
body.explanation: The axons of the retinal ganglion cells join together and leave the eye at the optic disc to form the optic nerve.

title: Which are stated functions of the vitreous humour? (choose all)
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which are stated functions of the vitreous humour? (choose all)
options: Holding the retina and lens in place
Refracting light at the eye's surface
body.explanation: The vitreous body is a watery jelly filling about 80 percent of the posterior segment. It transmits light and holds the retina and lens in their respective places. It is also called the postremal or vitreous chamber.

title: Which structure is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which structure is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to the lateral geniculate nucleus. The fully labelled diagram is on the Visual tab.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Choroid plexus. Capillary network lined by ependymal cells; makes most of the CSF (about 500 mL a day) and forms the blood-CSF barrier.
option_notes: Not at the arrow; this is the venous sinus along the top of the falx, where CSF drains.
This is at the arrow: the vascular tufts in the ventricles that make CSF.
Not at the arrow; this is the narrow midline cavity between the two thalami.
Not at the arrow; this is the narrow channel through the midbrain from the third to the fourth ventricle.

title: Which tract carries pain and temperature?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which tract carries pain and temperature?
body.explanation: Ascending: dorsal columns (fine touch, proprioception) and anterolateral spinothalamic tracts (pain, temperature). Descending: corticospinal (voluntary movement) and vestibulospinal (balance, posture).
option_notes: Touch and position sense.
Motor.
Spinothalamic: pain and temperature.
Posture, motor.

title: Which landmark marks the posterior border between the pons and the medulla on the floor of the fourth ventricle?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which landmark marks the posterior border between the pons and the medulla on the floor of the fourth ventricle?
options: The stria medullaris of the fourth ventricle
body.explanation: The stria medullaris crosses the floor transversely and marks the pons-medulla border.
option_notes: It marks the pons-medulla border.
The facial colliculus is on the pontine part.
The obex is the lowest tip.
The median eminence marks the midline.

title: What is the pyramidal lobe?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What is the pyramidal lobe?
options: A constant third lobe behind the trachea
The upper pole of each lateral lobe
A part of the parathyroid gland
body.explanation: From the upper edge of the isthmus, to the left of the median line, an inconstant extension of variable length stands out: the pyramidal lobe.
option_notes: It is neither constant nor behind the trachea.
It is not the upper pole.
Not parathyroid tissue.
It rises from the isthmus, a remnant of the thyroglossal duct.

title: Which nerve supplies most pharyngeal muscles?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: Which nerve supplies most pharyngeal muscles?
body.explanation: The vagus innervates all the muscles of the pharynx and soft palate except the tensor veli palatini (CN V3) and the stylopharyngeus (CN IX).

title: What do afferent nerves do?
subject: subj:anat3

body.stem: What do afferent nerves do?
body.explanation: Afferent nerves bring information to the CNS; efferent nerves carry signals from the CNS to organs and muscles.
